The build reads no original ROM: every input is in the repository, so the outputs are rebuilt from source rather than combined with extracted assets. The repository therefore carries the game's text, graphics and data in source form.

INSTALL.md covers Linux distributions, macOS with Homebrew, Windows through WSL (or Cygwin on older Windows) and Termux. The build needs make, gcc or clang, git and rgbds 1.0.4, which the repository pins; helper tools under tools/ handle graphics conversion, compression and patch generation.

make compare builds every target and runs sha1sum against roms.sha1. pret's CI does this on Linux and macOS with rgbds 1.0.4 and fails when the build leaves uncommitted changes, while forks only build. Matching hashes show identical output bytes, not that labels and documentation are complete or that modified builds behave correctly. This collection did not build the ROMs.

The repository has no license file, so reuse terms for the disassembly are unstated, and the original game's content remains its rights holders'. rgbds is a separate project with its own terms. The reviewed sources establish no AI or REA attribution.

name: Lighthouse: a Banjo-Kazooie PC port built on the decompilation
description_en: A native Windows, Linux and macOS port of Banjo-Kazooie that compiles game C sources, many tagged with their Banjo-Kazooie decompilation file paths, against libultraship, a reimplementation of the N64 SDK. Torch extracts the user’s ROM into an asset archive, and the port adds Anchor multiplayer, romhack and language-pack support and a randomizer. Unlike Banjo: Recompiled, it builds from decompiled source rather than statically recompiling the ROM’s code.
description_zh: 一个面向 Windows、Linux 和 macOS 的《Banjo-Kazooie》原生移植，将游戏 C 源码（其中许多标注了《Banjo-Kazooie》反编译项目中的文件路径）与重新实现 N64 SDK 的 libultraship 一起编译。Torch 将用户的 ROM 提取为素材归档；移植版还加入了 Anchor 联机、ROM 修改版与语言包支持以及随机器。与 Banjo: Recompiled 不同，它基于反编译源码构建，而非对 ROM 代码进行静态重编译。
requirements: Requires a supported retail ROM in .z64 form, identified by SHA-1 in the README: US 1.0, US 1.1, Japanese or PAL. It is extracted into a local bk.o2r archive; other regions can be added as language packs, and romhacks need the US 1.0 base. The repository includes no copyrighted game assets.
Release 1.1.0 “Hatteras Alfa” (2026-08-17) ships Windows x64, Linux and macOS archives. Rendering backends are DirectX 11 (Windows default), OpenGL on all platforms and Metal (macOS default).

Source builds need the libultraship and Torch submodules and CMake, plus Visual Studio 2022 (MSVC v143), Python 3 and at least 8 GB RAM on Windows, GCC or Clang with Ninja and the listed SDL2, libzip, tinyxml2, spdlog, Boost and Vorbis packages on Linux, or Xcode and the listed packages on macOS. Build targets extract bk.o2r from the ROM and package port assets as lighthouse.o2r.
The README publishes no matching or fidelity checks. Most supported romhacks are not fully tested, and CI nightly builds are for playtesting and may crash; nothing was built or run here.

The repository is dedicated under CC0 1.0; submodules keep their own licenses, and the game is not covered. The README discloses AI assistance for information gathering and accepts AI-assisted pull requests under the HarbourMasters policy; no REA use is documented.

name: Lost Odyssey Recomp: statically recompiling an Xbox 360 RPG into native ports
description_en: Translates Lost Odyssey’s Xbox 360 PowerPC executable with patched XenonRecomp tooling and runs the generated code on a native runtime that renders through Direct3D 12, Vulkan or Metal. Windows, Linux, macOS and Android packages import the user’s own disc data. The maintainer documents development with Claude Code and Codex CLI and records each release separately from validation and acceptance.
description_zh: 使用打过补丁的 XenonRecomp 工具转换 Lost Odyssey 的 Xbox 360 PowerPC 可执行文件，并在原生运行时上运行生成代码，经 Direct3D 12、Vulkan 或 Metal 渲染。Windows、Linux、macOS 和 Android 安装包导入使用者自己的光盘数据。维护者记录了借助 Claude Code 与 Codex CLI 的开发过程，并把每次发布与验证、验收分开记录。
requirements: The reviewed main snapshot follows v1.0.4 (2026-10-18), packaged for Windows x64 with AVX, Linux x64 AppImage/Flatpak, macOS 15+ on Apple Silicon and 64-bit Android 8.0+ with Vulkan. STATUS.md and ROADMAP.md record each release as published but not accepted by the maintainer. This is static recompilation of the shipped executable, not recovered authored source or a general Xbox 360 emulator.

Players import data from one supported four-disc set, Asian multilingual or USA/Europe (Title ID 4D5307FA); Disc 1 is required, DLC is optional, and other regions, title updates and modified XEX files are unsupported. Source builds use the Asian multilingual Disc 1 default.xex, LO.fpi and resource archives, and BUILDING.md still calls four-disc integration incomplete. Game data and generated code are kept out of the repository.

Builds need submodules including XenonRecomp, XenosRecomp, plume and SDL 3, with project patches applied, plus Python 3.11+, CMake 3.28+, Ninja and Clang: clang-cl with Visual Studio 2022 Build Tools on Windows 10 1803+, or Clang/LLD with a Vulkan driver on Linux. tools/ppc_codegen.py regenerates the guest sources locally before the runtime build.

STATUS.md separates implementation, validation, acceptance and release; for example, v1.0.4’s save fix passed a logic review, a CPU fixture and a Release link but was not run in-game. Upscaler and rendering checks name bounded fixtures and GPUs. The workflow guide states that a release does not mean the game was completed start to finish; this collection ran nothing.

GPL-3.0 covers project code; Lost Odyssey and its assets belong to their owners, and dependencies such as the Xenia FFmpeg fork, DXC, optional DLSS/FSR/XeSS SDKs and Android GPU drivers keep their own terms. docs/AI_WORKFLOW.md says one maintainer used Claude Code as the main session with Codex CLI and subagents; Ghidra scripts and a third-party reverse-engineering skill are referenced, but no REA use is established.

name: Super Smash Bros. Melee: a matching GameCube decompilation with a shiftable build
description_en: A matching decompilation of Super Smash Bros. Melee's US 1.02 release (GALE01) that rebuilds main.dol from C with the original Metrowerks compilers and checks it against the retail SHA-1. decomp.dev reports the code fully decompiled and linked at the reviewed commit, and the README says current work is mostly naming and cleanup. Because the build can be shifted, a separate non-matching mode lets modders add code to a DOL run with their own disc dump.
description_zh: Super Smash Bros. Melee 美版 1.02（GALE01）的一致性反编译：使用原版 Metrowerks 编译器从 C 代码重建 main.dol，并与零售版的 SHA-1 比对。decomp.dev 报告所审提交的代码已完全反编译并链接，README 称目前工作主要是命名与清理。由于构建可以移位，另有非一致性模式，供模组作者加入代码，再配合自己转储的光盘运行生成的 DOL。
requirements: README describes a matching decompilation that builds the US 1.02 main.dol (game ID GALE01) with SHA-1 08e0bf20134dfcb260699671004527b2d6bb1a45, the digest config/GALE01/build.sha1 checks. decomp.dev reports 100.00% decompiled and 100.00% fully linked for this commit, and README says most effort now goes to naming and cleanup. The output is a GameCube DOL, not a PC executable; the CMake library and DWARF packages CI also builds are not documented as a playable port, and none is claimed here.

Supply main.dol from your own GALE01 disc; the repository's orig/GALE01 folders hold only placeholders. The README's modding path needs the whole disc dumped to a folder, enables configure.py --non-matching with new objects marked Equivalent, and runs the rebuilt DOL in Dolphin. Such modified builds are not byte-identical to retail and fall outside the matching result.

Host tools are Python and ninja on Windows (native tooling recommended), macOS (Game Porting Toolkit runs the Windows compilers) or Linux (WiBo on x86, Wine elsewhere). configure.py sets up decomp-toolkit, sjiswrap and the Metrowerks GC/1.2.5 and GC/1.1p1 compilers with the GC/1.3.2 linker; objdiff diffs objects and tools/decomp.py drafts functions with m2c. CI builds link, test and debug modes in a build container that provides the original files, plus a Nix matching build.

Matching rests on the linked DOL's SHA-1 and objdiff's per-unit report; CI's check_complete.py warns when a unit matches fully but is not yet marked complete. The 100% figures are decomp.dev's report for this commit; this collection did not build the DOL or rerun any comparison.

No repository-wide licence file is present at the reviewed commit and GitHub detects none; bundled tools under tools/ carry their own licences, and the game, its DOL and assets keep their rights holders' terms. CONTRIBUTING.md says using AI to match functions is acceptable and frequently practiced, while asking contributors not to let AI name struct fields or global identifiers or attempt data-section matches. No REA use is documented and no runtime reproduction is claimed.

name: pokecrystal: a matching Pokémon Crystal disassembly
description_en: Reconstructs the Game Boy Color game Pokémon Crystal as RGBDS assembly, with graphics, maps and data stored as editable sources. One tree builds the international 1.0 and 1.1 releases, the Australian release, two debug builds and a Virtual Console patch, each checked against a recorded SHA-1. Companion documentation covers script command formats and known bugs in the original game.
description_zh: 以 RGBDS 汇编重建 Game Boy Color 游戏《精灵宝可梦 水晶》，图像、地图和数据以可编辑的源文件保存。同一源码树可构建国际版 1.0 与 1.1、澳大利亚版、两个调试构建以及一个 Virtual Console 补丁，并逐一与记录的 SHA-1 比对。配套文档说明脚本命令格式以及原版游戏中的已知错误。
requirements: README lists six outputs with SHA-1s: Crystal (UE) 1.0 and 1.1, the Australian release, two debug builds and the CGBBYTE1.784 Virtual Console patch. Version differences are selected with assembler defines such as _CRYSTAL11 and _CRYSTAL_AU, and plain make builds only the 1.0 ROM. The Japanese release is not among the listed targets.

The build reads no original ROM: code, text, maps, audio, PNG graphics and other data are in the repository, including the mobile library code linked into the ROM. The repository therefore carries the game's content in source form. Packaging the Virtual Console patch into an installable title is outside the project's scope.

INSTALL.md covers Linux distributions, macOS with Homebrew, Windows through WSL (or Cygwin on older Windows) and Termux. The build needs make, gcc or clang, git and rgbds 1.0.4, which the repository pins; FAQ.md notes that rgbds releases before 1.0.0 fail.

make compare builds every target and runs sha1sum against roms.sha1. pret's CI does this on Linux and macOS with rgbds 1.0.4 and fails when the build leaves uncommitted changes, while forks only build. Bug and design-flaw notes describe fixes as optional diffs, since the matching build keeps the original behavior. This collection did not build the ROMs.

The repository has no license file, so reuse terms for the disassembly are unstated, and the original game's content remains its rights holders'. rgbds is a separate project with its own terms. The reviewed sources establish no AI or REA attribution.

name: Pokémon HeartGold and SoulSilver: a work-in-progress, checksum-matched DS disassembly
description_en: Rebuilds the US Nintendo DS releases of Pokémon HeartGold and SoulSilver from a work-in-progress disassembly in which part of the code has been decompiled to C. Each default build checks the ARM9 and ARM7 binaries, the filesystem and the complete ROM against per-game SHA-1 manifests. README warns that, because decompilation is incomplete, edits that change code or data layout can crash the game.
description_zh: 以进行中的反汇编项目重建美版 Nintendo DS《宝可梦 心金／魂银》，其中部分代码已反编译为 C。每次默认构建都会按各游戏的 SHA-1 清单校验 ARM9 与 ARM7 二进制、文件系统及完整 ROM。README 提醒，由于反编译尚未完成，改变代码或数据布局的修改可能导致游戏崩溃。
requirements: README calls this a work-in-progress disassembly of the US releases; it warns that symbol names and code structure can change, and that edits altering the size or layout of any function or data structure can crash the game because the ROM is not fully decompiled. At the reviewed commit asm/ still holds 283 assembly files beside 406 C files in src/, and CONTRIBUTING.md describes NONMATCHING C kept beside the inline-assembly versions used for matching builds. Outputs are pokeheartgold.us.nds and pokesoulsilver.us.nds, not a PC port.

The documented build reads no original ROM: the DS filesystem’s graphics, model, text and data files are committed under files/. The target images are identified by SHA-1 (HeartGold 4fcded0e2713dc03929845de631d0932ea2b5a37, SoulSilver f8dc38ea20c17541a43b58c5e6d18c1732c7e582), and README links their No-Intro records. Only the contributor asmdiff tool refers to a user-supplied base ROM.

INSTALL.md covers WSL2 (recommended), WSL1, MSYS2, macOS and Debian, Arch and Fedora Linux; packages include an ARM GCC toolchain, bison, flex, Ninja, Python 3, libpng and 32-bit libc, and macOS also needs Wine. The Makefile clones Meson 1.12.0 and downloads the metroskrew 0.1.3 release, which its repository describes as a relinked Linux port of the proprietary Windows Metrowerks ARM compiler; Meson fetches pinned NitroSDK, NitroSystem, NitroDWC, NitroWiFi and libvct subprojects. make builds HeartGold and make soulsilver builds SoulSilver.

make runs Meson tests after building that check the ARM9 main binary, ARM7 binary, filesystem and complete ROM against SHA-1 manifests; the Makefile tells modders they may drop that check after their first build. CI builds and checks both games and runs a progress calculation on pushes. Matching hashes establish identity for these two US images, not decompilation completeness or gameplay coverage; this collection did not build them.

The repository has no top-level license file and GitHub detects none; some bundled tools carry their own licenses, and the metroskrew and ntrtwl SDK repositories declare no license on GitHub. SDK libraries and original game content remain subject to their rights holders. CONTRIBUTING.md prohibits LLM-generated contributions apart from narrow, disclosed exceptions; the reviewed sources establish no AI or REA use in the project, and no runtime reproduction is claimed.

name: FFTARecomp: static recompilation of Final Fantasy Tactics Advance
description_en: Recompiles the user’s Final Fantasy Tactics Advance (USA) Game Boy Advance ROM ahead of time into native code for Windows, Linux and Steam Deck, building on JRickey’s gba-recomp toolkit. ARM and Thumb code is translated to C and compiled locally, while a Rust runtime models the console’s graphics, sound, DMA, timers and BIOS calls. The port adds widescreen, zoom, fast-forward and remappable controls.
description_zh: 基于 JRickey 的 gba-recomp 工具链，将使用者自有的 Final Fantasy Tactics Advance（美版）Game Boy Advance ROM 预先重编译为可在 Windows、Linux 和 Steam Deck 上运行的原生代码。ARM 与 Thumb 代码被转译为 C 并在本地编译，Rust 运行时则模拟主机的图形、声音、DMA、定时器及 BIOS 调用。移植另行加入宽屏、缩放、快进和可重映射操作。
requirements: Reviewed source follows the v2.0 release (2026-10-13) and is labelled a work in progress. README targets Windows 10/11, Linux and Steam Deck; its recomp manifest also lists Android and calls the game fully playable from start to finish. Without a C compiler the recompiler falls back to an interpreter, which upstream keeps for self-modifying code and as a differential-testing oracle. Known issues include brief sprite silhouettes in the first level and a gamepad that may go undetected on first launch.

Supply your own Final Fantasy Tactics Advance (USA) ROM, serial AFXE; the project manifest records the expected SHA-1. No console BIOS is needed, because BIOS calls are high-level emulated. The installer recompiles the game on the user’s PC, and the project excludes ROMs, saves, memory dumps and generated game C from its uploads.

Building from source needs Rust and Windows PowerShell (build-all.ps1). A C compiler is also a runtime requirement: the recompiler emits C11 and links a per-title library. The Windows installer downloads the w64devkit 2.10.0 GCC toolchain, and Linux release builds use Zig as a build-only cross compiler.

A dated release audit (2026-10-12) reports clean source-upload scans, 26 passing input-configuration and menu tests and successful Windows and Linux release builds, and leaves physical-controller behavior unmeasured. README cites no hardware or emulator comparison results; this collection ran nothing.

FFTARecomp changes are MIT and retain upstream gba-recomp notices (MIT OR Apache-2.0); gamedb.sqlite function metadata is CC0 1.0, and w64devkit tools keep their GPL-family licenses. The project’s audit does not establish logo and icon provenance, and Square Enix and Nintendo retain their game rights. Upstream gba-recomp describes itself as AI-assisted; no REA connection is established.

name: SymphonyRecomp: a RecompOne static recompilation of Symphony of the Night
description_en: Statically recompiles the North American PlayStation release of Castlevania: Symphony of the Night into C# with BlackLabelHQ’s RecompOne, whose runtime simulates the BIOS, memory-mapped I/O, GPU and CD-ROM so the game runs natively without a console BIOS. Per-overlay function maps and patches add widescreen, quality-of-life, randomizer and cheat features. References from the SOTN decompilation help name functions, but the project stresses that it is a recompilation, not a decompilation.
description_zh: 使用 BlackLabelHQ 的 RecompOne 将北美 PlayStation 版《恶魔城：月下夜想曲》静态重编译为 C#；其运行时模拟 BIOS、内存映射 I/O、GPU 和光驱，使游戏无需主机 BIOS 即可原生运行。按覆盖段划分的函数映射与补丁加入了宽屏、便利性改进、随机器和作弊功能。项目借助 SOTN 反编译项目的资料为函数命名，但强调它是重编译而非反编译。
requirements: Requires the user’s own North American disc (serial SLUS-00067) as a two-track BIN/CUE set or CHD with fixed file names; other-language discs are described only as future sources for a language switcher. The repository contains no game data, and RecompOne needs no BIOS or other Sony components.

Release v0.5.1b (2026-08-19) ships Windows x64/ARM64, macOS ARM64/x64 and Linux x64 builds; Linux ARM64 was dropped in 0.5b. Source-build prerequisites list an OpenGL 2.1+ GPU, .NET 10, OpenAL and Git, and the changelog calls the OpenGL 2.1 path experimental with bitmasking problems. Game code is generated by running the RecompOne submodule against config/sotn.json.

The README calls this an open beta that may contain game-breaking bugs, and 1.0 has not been released. No equivalence or automated gameplay test is published, and none of the changelog’s fixes or features was rerun here.

SymphonyRecomp has no license file, so reuse terms are unspecified; the pinned RecompOne recompiler and runtime are MIT-licensed, and the game retains its own rights. Both projects state that no AI was used to write their code and reject AI-generated pull requests; no REA use is established.

name: The Two Towers Recompiled: an original Xbox static-recompilation port
description_en: Statically recompiles the x86 code of The Lord of the Rings: The Two Towers (Xbox, USA, 2002) into C with the bundled xboxrecomp toolkit, producing native Windows, Linux and experimental macOS builds. The recompiled sources are generated locally from the player's own default.xbe, and game data comes from their disc image or extracted folder. README reports the game as fully playable, with visual, frame-rate and mod issues listed.
description_zh: 使用随附的 xboxrecomp 工具包，将《The Lord of the Rings: The Two Towers》（Xbox 美版，2002）的 x86 代码静态重编译为 C，生成原生 Windows、Linux 及实验性 macOS 构建。重编译源码由玩家自己的 default.xbe 在本地生成，游戏数据来自其光盘镜像或已提取的文件夹。README 报告游戏可以完整游玩，并列出画面、帧率和模组方面的问题。
requirements: README for v1.9.2 calls the port a fully playable work in progress and recommends 60 FPS; unlocked frame rates and widescreen are experimental. Downloads cover 64-bit Windows 7 SP1 to 11, x86-64 Linux with glibc 2.27+, and macOS 10.15+ on Intel or through Rosetta 2, with the macOS build not yet tested on a Mac. Known issues include stretched character shadows, lighting glitches, Vulkan black screens and several problems with the bundled extra-heroes mod.

Players need their own USA Xbox disc image or extracted game folder, and no game data is included. generate.py checks the retail default.xbe against a fixed SHA-256, then runs the xboxrecomp pipeline (XBE parsing, disassembly, function identification, ABI analysis, naming and recompilation) to write the C sources locally, so no recompiled code is committed. A separately distributed GameCube high-resolution texture pack is optional and not part of the release.

The repository vendors the xboxrecomp 0.12.0 static-recompilation toolkit, which translates an XBE's x86 code into C, and CHANGES.md lists the fixes made to it for this game. The game project builds with CMake 3.20+ and C11 under MSVC, MinGW or Clang/GCC; Linux uses SDL2 with OpenGL loaded at run time, and the renderer options are Direct3D 11, Vulkan through DXVK or OpenGL. The README at this revision has no build section; generate.py only says to build with CMake afterwards.

Testing reported for 1.9.2 covers menus, level loading and fonts in several languages under Wine and on Linux with OpenGL, and states that the Windows, Linux and macOS builds compile. No automated tests or CI runs are recorded for the reviewed commit, and this collection did not download releases or rerun anything.

LICENSE.txt applies MIT to the port's own code (twotowers/ and generate.py); the vendored xboxrecomp keeps MIT plus LGPL-2.1-or-later for parts taken from xemu. The license adds that the release's game program contains code mechanically translated from the original executable, which it does not cover and which remains the rights holders' property. Reviewed sources establish no REA involvement, and no runtime reproduction is claimed.

name: Melee Unlocked: a Windows source port and static recompilation of Melee
description_en: A beta Windows build of Super Smash Bros. Melee (NTSC 1.02) with two engines: a source port that compiles the doldecomp decompilation as a native library, and a static recompilation that translates the retail DOL's PowerPC code and Slippi's Gecko codes into C++. Both run on a native runtime with Direct3D rendering, unlocked display rates and natively implemented Slippi rollback play. The user's own ISO supplies all game data, and the README says the work was AI-assisted.
description_zh: Super Smash Bros. Melee（NTSC 1.02）的 Windows 测试版构建，包含两套引擎：源码移植将 doldecomp 反编译编译为原生库，静态重编译则将零售版 DOL 的 PowerPC 代码及 Slippi 的 Gecko 代码转换为 C++。两者都运行在原生运行时上，提供 Direct3D 渲染、解锁的显示帧率和原生实现的 Slippi 回滚对战。全部游戏数据来自使用者自备的 ISO，README 称开发借助了 AI。
requirements: README describes a beta Windows build with two engines chosen in the launcher. The Source Port compiles doldecomp/melee (a submodule pinned at 039c4bf plus a tracked native patch) into melee_game.dll on a native runtime with Direct3D 12/11 rendering, a mixer and direct controller input. The Static Recomp uses the project's Python recompiler to translate the retail DOL's PowerPC code and Slippi's Gecko codes ahead of time into C++, over HLE of the GameCube SDK. Game logic stays at 60 Hz while the display interpolates from animation data; VERSION and the latest release are 0.8.99, though README still names 0.8.76.

Supply your own Melee NTSC 1.02 ISO: the game reads its data from it, and the from-source build takes the retail main.dol from it as the recompiler's input. Nothing from the disc is committed or shipped. Online play needs a Slippi account through the Slippi Launcher; the optional DLSS 5 path needs NVIDIA's separately supplied runtime and model.

Windows 10/11 only. The Static Recomp build uses Python, CMake and the Visual Studio 2022 Build Tools (play.bat can install them with winget). The Source Port additionally needs MinGW-w64 GCC 14 or newer with Ninja for the game DLL, an MSVC-built host, and the same guest-translation step; it pins the doldecomp/melee and encounter/aurora submodules and applies its patch with a checking script.

README lists CTest unit tests, a validator requiring 2,400 simulation checkpoints to match across headless, hidden, threaded and authored rendering, and a two-instance Slippi match that must log no DESYNC. docs/replay-validation.md compares replays frame by frame in eight Slippi post-frame fields and says this does not establish equality of the complete game state; PORT_COMPLETION.md makes resolving a differing replay byte a precondition for claiming deterministic online compatibility. These are project-reported; nothing was run here.

GPL-3.0-or-later from 0.8.5 (GPL-2.0-or-later through 0.8.1); NOTICE lists code ported from Dolphin, Slippi Ishiiruka and Slippi, bundled components with their own licences, and a GPL section 7 permission for NVIDIA and Intel SDKs. Melee belongs to Nintendo and HAL Laboratory, and the project is unaffiliated with the Slippi team. README says it was developed with Fable 5.1 and GPT 6 Astra, and PORT_COMPLETION.md names Fable and Codex working branches; no REA use is documented and no runtime reproduction is claimed.

name: pokeruby: a matching Pokémon Ruby and Sapphire decompilation
description_en: Reconstructs the Game Boy Advance games Pokémon Ruby and Sapphire as C source built with pret's agbcc compiler, alongside assembly data scripts and editable graphics. Matching builds cover the English 1.0, 1.1 and 1.2 revisions, debug builds and the first German editions, each checked against a stored SHA-1. A separate modern-GCC target is not expected to match.
description_zh: 以 C 源码重建 Game Boy Advance 游戏《精灵宝可梦 红宝石／蓝宝石》，使用 pret 的 agbcc 编译器构建，并附有汇编数据脚本和可编辑图像。一致构建涵盖英文版 1.0、1.1、1.2 修订版、调试构建以及德文初版，并逐一与保存的 SHA-1 比对。另有使用现代 GCC 的构建目标，不以一致为目标。
requirements: README still calls the project a disassembly and lists hashes for English pokeruby.gba and pokesapphire.gba; INSTALL.md adds 1.1/1.2 revision targets, 1.0-only debug targets and first-edition German builds, and the tree holds 14 SHA-1 files. No asm/ directory remains in the reviewed tree: game code is C under src/, apart from handwritten startup and library assembly and functions marked NONMATCHING whose matching builds keep inline assembly. The contributor guide still describes the earlier asm-to-C workflow.

The build reads no original ROM: code, scripts, text, graphics and sound sources are in the repository, so the repository carries the game's content in source form. German builds need a setup script before compiling and a teardown script before any English build.

INSTALL.md lists Linux, macOS with Xcode Command Line Tools, and Windows through WSL or the devkitPro MSYS2 environment, plus build-essential, git, libpng and devkitARM. pret's agbcc must be cloned, built and installed into the tree; make modern uses devkitARM's arm-none-eabi-gcc instead, and other toolchains can be set with TOOLCHAIN.

With COMPARE=1 the Makefile checks the selected build against its SHA-1 file. The GitHub Actions workflow compares the English 1.0/1.1/1.2 Ruby and Sapphire builds and German first-edition variants, then compiles the NONMATCHING sources and the modern target without comparison; README's build badge still points to Travis CI. Matching hashes show identical ROM bytes, not that NONMATCHING C or modern builds behave identically. This collection did not build the ROMs.

No license file is present, so reuse terms are unstated; the original game's content remains its rights holders', and agbcc and devkitPro components keep their own terms. The reviewed sources establish no AI or REA attribution.

name: Vandal Hearts: native PC port built on matching decompilations
description_en: Builds on shao113’s matching decompilation of PlayStation Vandal Hearts, adds a Japanese matching tree, and carries both through to a native Windows and Linux port. SDL2, OpenGL or Metal and OpenAL backends replace the console’s GPU, GTE, CD-ROM/XA, SPU, MDEC and pad interfaces, and one executable runs the USA, Asia and Japan discs. The matching builds are still checked on every change; PC-only features such as Tactical Mode and HD packs are opt-in.
description_zh: 以 shao113 的 PlayStation 版 Vandal Hearts 一致性反编译为基础，新增日版一致性代码树，并将两者延伸为原生 Windows 与 Linux 移植。SDL2、OpenGL 或 Metal 及 OpenAL 后端替代主机的 GPU、GTE、CD-ROM／XA、SPU、MDEC 和手柄接口，同一可执行文件可运行美版、亚洲版和日版光盘。每次修改仍须通过一致性构建检查；Tactical Mode、高清包等 PC 专属功能均为可选。
requirements: Reviewed source follows v2.1.0 (2026-08-31). README reports every non-PsyQ function decompiled, with make check confirming byte-identical rebuilds of the US SLUS_004.47 and, since 2.0.0, the Japanese SLPM_860.07 by MD5, and full playthroughs through the endgame on Windows and Linux. macOS is a community-supported experimental build tested through the first battle; its full-playthrough and notarisation validation are pending.

Supply your own raw .bin disc image of the USA (SLUS-00447), Asia (SCPS-45183) or Japan (SLPM-86007) release; the port verifies and auto-detects each disc. The matching build also needs the original executable as its MD5 reference and locally sourced proprietary PsyQ SDK files (README lists ASPSX 2.21 and LIB34.ZIP by MD5). The kanji font, in-game text and static data segment are generated from the user’s copy, not committed.

The port builds with Make or CMake against SDL2, OpenAL, OpenGL (Metal on macOS), libwebp, libav and Python 3; Windows binaries are cross-compiled from Linux with MinGW-w64, and Linux ships as an AppImage. The matching build uses splat, maspsx, decompals’ GCC 2.5.7/2.6.3 frontends and MIPS binutils, and needs a Linux host because those frontends are 32-bit Linux executables.

Project-reported checks include make check for both regions, AddressSanitizer and UBSan sweeps that fixed seven latent out-of-bounds bugs, audio/visual fidelity validated against BizHawk, and a software rasterizer reported 99.84–99.99% pixel-exact against DuckStation VRAM captures. The known-issues list places remaining defects in the port’s rendering and backend layer; this collection ran none of these checks.

GPL-2.0 covers only the project’s original port code, tooling and documentation. The decompiled game code, derived from shao113’s unlicensed decompilation, and the reconstructed data tables are Konami’s and are not licensed by the project; pre-built releases embed part of the game-derived data segment and a BIOS-derived font. The repository keeps its setup recipe in Claude Code skill files; no REA connection is established.

name: Pokémon Platinum: a checksum-matched Nintendo DS decompilation
description_en: Reconstructs the US Nintendo DS release of Pokémon Platinum as C source that rebuilds revision 1 by default and revision 0 on request. The default make target runs Meson checks of the code binaries, filesystem and complete ROM against SHA-1 manifests. README still calls the project work in progress; its contributing guide says the code is entirely C but much of it remains obfuscated, leaving documentation and tooling as the main work.
description_zh: 将美版 Nintendo DS《宝可梦 白金》重建为 C 源码，默认重建修订版 1，也可按需构建修订版 0。默认的 make 目标会运行 Meson 检查，按 SHA-1 清单校验代码二进制、文件系统及完整 ROM。README 仍称项目在进行中；贡献指南表示代码已全部为 C，但其中大量仍晦涩难懂，因此主要工作是文档和工具。
requirements: README calls this a WIP decompilation of US Pokémon Platinum. CONTRIBUTING.md states that the repository is 100% C code, although much of it is obfuscated, so current work is mainly documentation and tooling; at the reviewed commit asm/ holds only macro includes beside 1,013 C files in src/. Outputs are pokeplatinum.us.nds ROM images, not a PC port.

The documented build reads no original ROM: graphics, sound, text and data sources, including some prebuilt data, are committed under res/. Revision 1, the default, has SHA-1 0862ec35b24de5c7e2dcb88c9eea0873110d755c; ROM_REVISION=0 builds revision 0, SHA-1 ce81046eda7d232513069519cb2085349896dec7, which INSTALL.md describes as the original North American retail version with a GTS level-range display error that a later shipment patched. README links both No-Intro records.

INSTALL.md covers WSL2 (recommended), WSL1, MSYS2, macOS and Debian, Arch and Fedora Linux; packages include an ARM GCC toolchain, bison, flex, Ninja, Python 3, libpng and 32-bit libc, and macOS also needs Wine. The Makefile clones Meson 1.12.0 and downloads the metroskrew 0.1.3 release, which its repository describes as a relinked Linux port of the proprietary Windows Metrowerks ARM compiler; Meson fetches pinned NitroSDK, NitroSystem, NitroDWC, NitroWiFi and libvct subprojects. make debug builds a GDB-enabled ROM, for which INSTALL.md points to an overlay-aware binutils-gdb fork.

make runs Meson tests that check shared, revision-specific and ARM7 binaries, the filesystem and the complete ROM against SHA-1 manifests; make rom skips the checksum when code is modified. CI installs metroskrew and runs make check for the default revision. Matching hashes establish identity for the listed US images, not gameplay coverage; this collection did not build them.

The repository has no top-level license file and GitHub detects none; some bundled tools carry their own licenses, and the metroskrew and ntrtwl SDK repositories declare no license on GitHub. SDK libraries and original game content remain subject to their rights holders. The reviewed sources establish no AI or REA use, and no runtime reproduction is claimed.

name: Saints Reborn: a ReXGlue static recompilation of Saints Row
description_en: An unofficial native Windows port of Saints Row (Xbox 360, 2006) that statically recompiles the game's PowerPC executable to C++ for x86-64 with the ReXGlue SDK, which also reimplements the console's kernel, GPU (on Direct3D 12), audio and input. A recompiler manifest, game-specific function overrides and an SDK patch make the result run, and each user builds it locally from their own disc. The README reports the game fully playable with built-in co-op and lists known issues.
description_zh: Saints Row（Xbox 360，2006）的非官方原生 Windows 移植：借助 ReXGlue SDK 将游戏的 PowerPC 可执行文件静态重编译为面向 x86-64 的 C++ 代码，该 SDK 还重新实现了主机的内核、GPU（基于 Direct3D 12）、音频与输入。重编译清单、游戏专用的函数替换和 SDK 补丁使结果得以运行，每位使用者都用自己的光盘在本地构建。README 报告游戏可完整通关、内置合作模式，并列出已知问题。
requirements: README describes a static recompilation, not a decompilation or an emulator: the ReXGlue SDK, pinned at v0.10.0 (commit c94f5eb) and patched by patches/rexglue-sdk.patch, translates every PowerPC function in default.xex to C++. config/saintsrow_manifest.toml adds ABI helpers, 19 functions reached only through vtables and two mid-function hooks, and project/src overrides rendering (predicated tiling), audio, kernel-object and occlusion-query behaviour. README reports the game fully playable from start to finish, with co-op over LAN, direct IP or a join code, an optional 60 FPS mod and a mod loader; known issues include texture flicker in the character creator.

Supply your own Saints Row (Xbox 360) disc as an .iso, or a game folder containing default.xex and packfiles. Only the disc version the port was made with is supported: setup compares default.xex with one known SHA-1 for the World disc release and warns otherwise, because the hooks use fixed addresses. The repository contains no game code, data, recompiled output or executables, and its legal notice forbids using it to distribute them.

Windows 10/11 (64-bit) with a Direct3D 12 GPU, about 15 GB of disk space and 16 GB of RAM. Setup downloads a portable clang, CMake, Ninja and Microsoft's C++ headers and libraries (about 1.5 GB) and builds the game locally in 10–60 minutes; the older setup.bat path needs Visual Studio 2022 with its Clang and CMake components, plus Git. README lists Linux (through Proton) as coming soon, although BUILDING.md already describes Setup as working on Windows and Linux.

Playability and the known-issue list are the author's reports. The only CI workflow builds the setup application; the repository's tests cover co-op, modding and map tools, and no automated comparison of recompiled behaviour against the console is documented. This collection did not build or run the port.

Project code is Apache-2.0 with a NOTICE that redistributors must keep, crediting Saints Reborn by Whompay. The SDK patch keeps the ReXGlue SDK's BSD-style licence, the SDK derives in part from Xenia, and libraries downloaded at build time keep their own terms. Saints Row remains its owners' property, and the NOTICE covers no file extracted or generated from the game. The reviewed sources establish no AI or REA attribution, and no runtime reproduction is claimed.

name: Pokémon Platinum PC Port: a native port built on the pret decompilation
description_en: Builds native 64-bit Windows and Linux executables of Pokémon Platinum from a fork of pret’s decompilation, replacing NitroSDK with the author’s libntr libraries; the same tree keeps the DS ROM build and an experimental Switch target. README says the game should be playable from start to finish but may crash or show graphical bugs. Prebuilt binaries require the player’s own US ROM, and the fork’s default build no longer runs pret’s checksum tests.
description_zh: 基于 pret 反编译项目的分支，为《宝可梦 白金》构建原生 64 位 Windows 和 Linux 可执行文件，并以作者的 libntr 库替代 NitroSDK；同一源码树仍保留 DS ROM 构建和实验性的 Switch 目标。README 称游戏应可从头玩到尾，但可能出现崩溃和图形错误。预构建程序需要玩家自备美版 ROM，且该分支的默认构建不再运行 pret 的校验测试。
requirements: README describes an experimental PC port of US Pokémon Platinum based on pret’s decompilation, using libntr, libntrsystem, libntrwifi and libntrdwc in place of NitroSDK and related DS libraries. The Meson build_target option selects arm (DS ROM), linux, win64 or nx, and README calls the NX target working but slow. Its goals of full WiFi and multiplayer support and later homebrew console ports are stated aims, not verified features.

README requires users of the prebuilt release binaries to supply their own dumped US Platinum ROM (game code CPUE01), selected on first launch; only the US version is supported. The source tree keeps pret’s committed res/ data, and README asks forks not to publish releases that bundle compiled assets with PC binaries.

Linux builds are recommended through the Docker wrapper drun.sh; a non-container build on Arch Linux lists nasm, enet, arm-none-eabi-gcc, Ninja, flex and bison. Windows uses PowerShell scripts that create a portable MSYS2 environment before make win64, and the NX target needs devkitA64. The ARM and Linux CI jobs install the inherited metroskrew Metrowerks compiler, and the libntr subprojects track their main branches rather than pinned revisions.

CI builds the ARM ROM, Linux and Windows targets on pc_port pushes and packages Linux and Windows artifacts; the latest release, v0.1.12 (2026-10-10), ships Linux and Windows zip archives from a commit earlier than the reviewed one. The fork’s default make target drops pret’s checksum dependency and CI does not run make check, so the reviewed sources do not show that its DS ROM still matches retail or that the PC build behaves identically. This collection ran neither build.

The fork has no top-level license file and GitHub detects none; libntr declares MIT, which README says release publishers must honor, while pret’s decompilation declares no license and original game content remains subject to its rights holders. README states that generative AI/LLM shortcuts were not used and that AI-made pull requests are rejected, and AGENTS.md repeats that refusal. No REA use is established, and no runtime reproduction is claimed.

name: MikuPan: a native Fatal Frame PC port built on the Himuro decompilation
description_en: Ports the PS2 game Fatal Frame to native PC builds without emulation; its repository description names the Himuro decompilation as its basis. Stubs replace PS2 kernel calls and a new SDL3-based layer handles rendering, audio and UI, while game data comes from the user’s own disc. The README calls the port very early work and publishes no matching or fidelity checks.
description_zh: 将 PS2 游戏 Fatal Frame（《零》）移植为无需模拟器的原生 PC 版本；仓库简介称其基于 Himuro 反编译项目。PS2 内核调用由桩函数替代，渲染、音频和界面由基于 SDL3 的新层实现，游戏数据则来自使用者自有的光盘。README 称移植仍处于很早期阶段，未发布一致性或还原度检查。
requirements: README describes an in-progress native PC port of the PS2 game with no emulation and calls it very early work; debug builds are recommended because release builds have issues. Per the repository description its basis is Himuro, a separate decompilation aiming for matching US, EU and JP PS2 executables, and MikuPan’s game-code directories follow Himuro’s source layout. This record covers the port, not Himuro’s matching progress.

Requires IMG_HD.BIN and IMG_BD.BIN from an independently obtained Fatal Frame disc image of the matching region: NTSC-U for the default presets or PAL/EU for the *-eu presets. NTSC-J images are unsupported. The README states that the game data is not packaged, including in Android APKs.

Builds use CMake 3.28+ and C++20 and fetch SDL3, FFmpeg, SDL_shadercross and other libraries; Windows uses MinGW, Cygwin or MSVC, and Linux uses GCC. macOS is not officially supported, though contributors report Apple Silicon builds on SDL_GPU’s Metal backend. Android packaging needs Android SDK 35+, NDK r28c+ and prebuilt FFmpeg libraries.

CI builds Windows, Linux and macOS targets on pushes and pull requests and publishes nightly prerelease archives. The reviewed tree has no test suite, matching check or gameplay-comparison result, so behavioral parity with the PS2 game remains unverified; this collection did not build or run the port.

MikuPan declares AGPL-3.0 and Himuro declares MIT; bundled third-party binaries and libraries keep their own terms, and Fatal Frame data retains separate rights. The reviewed sources establish no AI or REA attribution, and no runtime reproduction is claimed.

name: Starfox 64: Recompiled — an N64Recomp static-recompilation port
description_en: Uses N64: Recompiled to statically recompile the US 1.1 (Rev A) Nintendo 64 release of Star Fox 64 into a native port for Windows, Linux and macOS, rendered with RT64. Its patches and enhancements draw on headers and some functions from the separate sf64 decompilation, but the port is not compiled from that decompilation's source. The README reports high-frame-rate, widescreen and mod support, with assets loaded from the user's own ROM.
description_zh: 使用 N64: Recompiled 将 Nintendo 64 版 Star Fox 64 美版 1.1（Rev A）静态重编译为面向 Windows、Linux 和 macOS 的原生移植，并以 RT64 渲染。补丁与增强功能借用独立的 sf64 反编译项目中的头文件和部分函数，但移植本身并非由该反编译源码编译而成。README 报告支持高帧率、宽屏与模组，素材从使用者自备的 ROM 载入。
requirements: README describes a static recompilation, not an emulator or a decompilation-based source port: N64Recomp translates the game code in the ROM (us.rev1.toml, with symbols from the Starfox64RecompSyms submodule) and RSPRecomp the audio microcode (aspMain.us.rev1.toml), running on N64ModernRuntime with RT64. Patches use headers and some functions from the sf64 decompilation submodule. README links release 1.0.3, the latest GitHub release (2025-12-30), lists planned features and one overlay-related known issue, and calls Starship a sibling port built with different technology.

Players provide the US 1.1 (Rev A) N64 ROM in the main menu; the port accepts only that ROM, converting other dump formats of it to .z64, and loads its assets from it. Building also needs a decompressed copy of the same ROM as recompiler input, identified in BUILDING.md by MD5. The repository and releases contain no game assets; CI copies the decompressed ROM from a private repository through secrets.

Runs on Windows, Linux (x64, ARM64, Flatpak, Steam Deck) and macOS 13 or newer, with a GPU supporting Direct3D 12 (Shader Model 6), Vulkan 1.2 or Metal Argument Buffers Tier 2, and SSE4.1 on x86-64. Building needs CMake, Ninja and clang (on Windows Visual Studio 2022 with its Clang and CMake components plus make; on Ubuntu SDL2, GTK 3, LLVM and lld), with N64Recomp and RSPRecomp built separately; CI pins N64Recomp at commit 98bf104.

The reviewed sources document features and nightly CI builds for Windows, macOS and Linux, not tests or comparisons of recompiled behaviour against the original. DOCS/fox_lore.md recounts the sf64 decompilation's matching history, which belongs to that separate project. This collection did not download builds or run anything.

COPYING is GPLv3; the original ROM and the bundled libraries keep their own terms. This is a static recompilation, not recovered authored source, and README credits the decompilation team's reverse engineering for the port's enhancements. The reviewed sources establish no AI or REA attribution, and no runtime reproduction is claimed.

name: Syphon Filter: The Omega Strain — matching PS2 executable decompilation
description_en: Reconstructs much of the NTSC-U PlayStation 2 executable of Syphon Filter: The Omega Strain as C; with the remaining functions kept as split assembly, the build reproduces the retail SCUS_972.64 byte for byte. Committed objdiff reports track per-function matching against the user’s own executable. This is a matching-decompilation case, not a PC port; progress figures remain project-reported.
description_zh: 将 Syphon Filter: The Omega Strain 北美版 PlayStation 2 可执行文件的大部分代码重建为 C；其余函数保留为拆分出的汇编，整体构建可逐字节重现零售版 SCUS_972.64。仓库提交的 objdiff 报告以使用者自备的可执行文件为基准，追踪逐函数的匹配进度。这是一致性反编译案例，不是 PC 移植；进度数字仍为项目报告。
requirements: Targets only the NTSC-U executable SCUS_972.64; the output is a rebuilt PS2 ELF, not a native PC program. At the reviewed commit, the committed objdiff report and handoff note list 13,413 of 14,331 functions (93.59%), 76.59% of code bytes and 99.92% of data as matched, with the rest still assembly. The dated status table in PROGRESS.md shows older, lower figures, and function totals shift as boundaries are refined.

Supply SCUS_972.64 from an independently owned disc or image; configure.py checks its SHA-256 against config/target.sha256 before splitting. No disc data, split assembly, objects or rebuilt executable is committed; derived files are generated in git-ignored folders. Executable data regions are committed as generated C definitions.

Setup needs Python 3.10+ with pinned splat 0.50.0 and spimdisasm 1.42.4, ninja, MIPS binutils and objdiff-cli. Windows runs the tools natively; Linux/macOS run the Windows compiler through wibo or wine. The setup script downloads a CodeWarrior PS2 3.0.3 build archived by decomp.me, but the licensed 3.0 build 38 and 3.04 build 22 installations used by per-unit overrides are not supplied; without them those units fall back to retail assembly. Library units use EE-GCC 2.95.3 and 2.96.

Verification is a whole-image SHA-256 comparison: ninja fails unless the rebuilt executable matches the retail hash, and the project claims a function match only with that check and objdiff identity. CI cannot build without the executable and only uploads the locally generated report for decomp.dev. The project treats build 38 compatibility as code-generation evidence, not proof of the original compiler; this collection did not rerun any build.

No license file is present at the reviewed commit, so reuse terms for the project’s code are unstated; the game, its executable and the proprietary Metrowerks compilers retain separate rights. The handoff note addresses a person or AI agent and the progress log plans parallel agent work, without attributing specific matches; no REA connection is established.

name: Animal Crossing: a native PC port of the GameCube decompilation
description_en: Runs Animal Crossing’s decompiled GameCube C code natively on 32-bit x86, replacing the GX graphics API with an OpenGL 3.3 translation layer and console services with SDL2-based platform code. Game assets are read at startup from the user’s own disc image instead of being shipped. It is a port built on ACreTeam’s ac-decomp, not a matching rebuild of the original executable.
description_zh: 让 Animal Crossing 反编译所得的 GameCube C 代码在 32 位 x86 上原生运行，用转换层把 GX 图形 API 映射到 OpenGL 3.3，并以基于 SDL2 的平台代码替代主机服务。游戏素材在启动时从使用者自己的光盘镜像读取，不随项目分发。这是基于 ACreTeam ac-decomp 的移植，而非与原可执行文件一致的重建。
requirements: The reviewed snapshot is the v0.9.3-playtest pre-release and supports only the USA Rev 0 release (GAFE01_00). The README calls the underlying ac-decomp complete, while the developer documentation calls it 99.52% complete; neither figure was checked here. Online play is not planned, and the Animal Crossing Deluxe mod is incompatible, although this release adapts some of its quality-of-life changes.

Requires the user’s own Animal Crossing (USA) disc image in ISO, GCM or CISO form; at startup the port loads main.dol, foresta.rel.szs and about 2,500 assets from it in memory. The README states that the repository contains no game assets or assembly. Saves use Dolphin-compatible GCI files, and optional HD texture packs use Dolphin’s naming format.

Windows is the primary target: the documented build uses an MSYS2 MINGW32 shell with 32-bit MinGW GCC, CMake 3.16+ and SDL2, plus vendored GLAD for an OpenGL 3.3 Core context. Builds must be 32-bit, unoptimized (-O0) and define NDEBUG, because the decompiled code casts pointers to 32-bit values and contains optimization-sensitive undefined behavior. Linux i686 is described as compiling and linking but is not officially supported.

About 100 decompilation files carry TARGET_PC changes, and optional PC_ENHANCEMENTS add settings, MSAA and texture-pack loading. The project describes Windows as fully tested and records an unresolved bass-distortion audio issue, but publishes no automated tests or byte-matching checks for the port. Equivalence with the GameCube original is not established, and this review did not build or run it.

LICENSE keeps the decompilation code under CC0 1.0 from ac-decomp and licenses the pc/ layer and TARGET_PC additions under MIT, with a separate MIT notice for FixNES; GitHub classifies no single license. Game content rights are separate. The README discloses that AI tools such as Claude were used for port code only; no REA use is established.

name: GoldenEye 007: matching Nintendo 64 decompilation for three releases
description_en: Reconstructs GoldenEye 007’s Nintendo 64 code as C source that rebuilds the US, Japanese and PAL ROMs. Assets come from a user-supplied US ROM, with Japanese and PAL differences taken from their own ROMs, and the default build compares each output with a recorded SHA-1. The README still calls the project work in progress, while a mutable status page reports all 208 files done; it is distinct from the separately curated PC port.
description_zh: 将 GoldenEye 007 的 Nintendo 64 代码重建为 C 源码，可重新构建美版、日版和 PAL 版 ROM。素材取自使用者自备的美版 ROM，日版与 PAL 版的差异部分则取自各自的 ROM；默认构建会将每个产物与记录的 SHA-1 比对。README 仍称项目在进行中，而可变的状态页报告全部 208 个文件已完成；它与另行收录的 PC 移植不同。
requirements: The reviewed GitHub repository describes itself as a mirror of the kholdfuzion GitLab project. README calls it a work-in-progress decompilation that builds US, JP and EU ROMs, each with a listed SHA-1. The mutable status page reports 208 of 208 files done and 100% for src, src/game, src/inflate and src/libultra without stating its unit. The output is an N64 ROM, not the separately curated native PC port.

Requires an unmodified, independently obtained US ROM; JP and PAL builds additionally need their own original ROMs, and US asset extraction must come first. The README states that the repository does not include all assets needed to compile the ROMs.

Documented hosts are Linux, WSL or a VM, plus Docker or Docker Compose. The build uses GNU make, MIPS binutils, Python 3 and host build tools. By default it compiles C with a locally generated static recompilation of the IRIX IDO 5.3 compiler from vendored decompals/ido-static-recomp; alternatively it runs the original IDO binaries under qemu-irix.

With the default COMPARE=1, the build checks the output ROM’s SHA-1 and prints an OK line for the selected version; COMPARE=0 and the DEBUG and USB variants skip that check, so they are not matching results. NTSC, JP and EU CI workflows build from secretly supplied base ROMs and generate status reports; this collection ran none of these checks.

GitHub detects no license and the reviewed tree has no top-level license file, so no reuse grant is established. Original ROMs and extracted assets retain separate rights, and the checked-in IRIX IDO binaries and vendored tools keep their own terms. The reviewed sources establish no AI or REA attribution, and no runtime reproduction is claimed.

name: Starship: a Star Fox 64 PC port built from the decompilation
description_en: A native PC port of Star Fox 64 that compiles the game's decompiled C code against libultraship, an N64 porting library that reimplements libultra and renders through Fast3D. On first run it uses the Torch tool to turn the user's US ROM into an asset archive, and it ships for Windows, Linux, macOS and Switch. The README of the separate Starfox 64: Recompiled static recompilation calls this port its sibling, built with different technology.
description_zh: Star Fox 64 的原生 PC 移植：将游戏的反编译 C 代码与 libultraship 一同编译，该 N64 移植库重新实现了 libultra，并通过 Fast3D 渲染。首次运行时借助 Torch 工具把使用者的美版 ROM 转换为素材资源包，提供 Windows、Linux、macOS 和 Switch 版本。独立的静态重编译项目 Starfox 64: Recompiled 在其 README 中称本移植为采用不同技术的姊妹项目。
requirements: Starship's README presents a PC port with release and playtest builds. DOCS/fox_lore.md in the sibling Starfox64Recomp repository describes it as a native port of the sf64 decompilation's C code on libultraship (which reimplements most of libultra and uses a Fast3D renderer) and says native porting exposed asset-linking errors and undefined behaviour that matching code alone did not reveal. CMakeLists.txt compiles src/engine, src/overlays, src/sys and src/audio with a port layer in src/port. The latest release is v2.0.0 (2025-05-25), and README warns that CI playtest builds will likely show bugs and possibly crashes.

Supply a US 1.0 or US 1.1 Rev A ROM in .z64 form; README lists the SHA-1 of each. The first run, or the ExtractAssets build target, turns it into sf64.o2r through Torch, using the definitions in config.yml and assets/yaml. JP and EU ROMs serve only as voice-language replacements alongside a US ROM, and the Switch build needs the archive generated on PC. The repository holds extraction definitions, not game assets.

Releases target Windows, Linux (AppImage), macOS and Nintendo Switch, with DirectX 11, OpenGL and Metal back ends. Building needs CMake, Python 3 and Git with Visual Studio 2022 (v143 tools; at least 8 GB of RAM) on Windows, or gcc or clang with Ninja and libraries including SDL2, libzip, spdlog, tinyxml2, Boost and Ogg/Vorbis on Linux. Submodules are libultraship, Torch and asm-differ; CI generates only the port's own starship.o2r and packages builds without a ROM.

Neither README nor BUILDING.md documents automated gameplay tests or comparisons with the original game, and the decompilation's matching status belongs to the separate sf64 project. This collection did not download builds or run anything.

LICENSE.md is CC0 1.0 Universal; the ROM, extracted assets and the game remain their owners' property, and the submodules keep their own terms. README says the project does not condone piracy. The reviewed sources establish no AI or REA attribution, and no runtime reproduction is claimed.

name: CTR Turbocharged: a PC sourceport built on the Crash Team Racing decompilation
description_en: Extends the Crash Team Racing: High Octane sourceport, which derives from the CTR Native port of the CTR-ModSDK PlayStation decompilation, into Windows and Linux builds with a native 3D renderer, selectable aspect ratios and frame rates up to 240 FPS. The decompiled game code still assumes 32-bit pointers and loads assets from the player’s own NTSC-U disc image. Renderer, timing and option tests exist, but device coverage and fidelity remain project-reported.
description_zh: 在 Crash Team Racing: High Octane 移植版基础上扩展而成；High Octane 源自基于 CTR-ModSDK PlayStation 反编译成果的 CTR Native 移植。本分支面向 Windows 与 Linux，提供原生 3D 渲染器、可选画面比例及最高 240 FPS 帧率。反编译游戏代码仍假定 32 位指针，并从玩家自备的 NTSC-U 光盘镜像读取素材。项目附有渲染、计时和选项测试，但设备覆盖与还原度仍为项目自述。
requirements: The reviewed turbocharged branch (VERSION 2026.10.1) forks High Octane v1.4.1, which builds on CTR Native and the CTR-ModSDK decompilation. It is a source port of decompiled C, not a matching decompilation or a static recompilation. Only Windows and Linux PC builds are supported; the inherited PS Vita and web builds are not, and the online leaderboard and Discord Rich Presence are disabled.

Game data is not included. The player supplies a raw MODE2/2352 BIN image of the NTSC-U (US) retail Crash Team Racing disc, used as assets/ctr-u.bin; 2048-byte ISO images and CUE files are not accepted. The first-run importer checks sector layout, the NTSC-U executable and boot configuration, required files and the audio manifest, but does not compare the image against a retail checksum. Optional PAL voiceovers and custom characters need a PAL or NTSC-U disc image and the project’s Python tools.

Builds must target 32-bit x86 because the decompiled code assumes 4-byte pointers. The documented CMake 3.20+ presets cover Linux gcc-multilib, Windows MinGW32/MSYS2 and Visual Studio 2022, with SDL3 and other dependencies vendored; Linux builds also need 32-bit X11, OpenGL, audio, udev and D-Bus development packages. Running needs an OpenGL 3.3 GPU and driver, plus 32-bit runtime libraries on Linux.

README reports 31 CTest tests with renderer tests enabled: 25 display-independent and 6 needing an OpenGL context. CI runs the display-independent subset on Linux and Windows and the GPU subset under Xvfb with software GL, which may skip without a context. The tested-devices table confirms one Linux setup and no Windows machine, and known issues include Wayland problems with 32-bit libraries. These are project reports, not byte-matching or gameplay-equivalence results; this collection did not run them.

The repository is GPLv3. Its third-party notices record PsyCross-derived platform code (MIT), PSn00bSDK headers (MPL 2.0), SDL and other vendored components under their own licenses, and the bundled fonts keep Apache 2.0 and OFL terms. Contributing rules keep retail disc data and extracted assets out of commits; the original game remains its owners’ property. The reviewed sources state no AI or REA use.

name: The Darkness Recomp: an Xbox 360 static recompilation with a native D3D11 renderer
description_en: Builds a native Windows x64 port of The Darkness by translating its Xbox 360 executable to C++ ahead of time with a patched XenonRecomp. A D3D11 renderer draws from the engine’s original geometry, shader sources and device state instead of interpreting console GPU packets. Gameplay coverage and Linux results are project-reported, and the author discloses OpenAI Codex assistance.
description_zh: 使用打过补丁的 XenonRecomp 将 Xbox 360 可执行文件提前转换为 C++，构建 The Darkness 的原生 Windows x64 移植。D3D11 渲染器直接使用引擎原有的几何数据、着色器源码和设备状态绘制，而不解释主机 GPU 命令包。游戏覆盖范围与 Linux 测试结果均为项目报告，作者披露开发中使用了 OpenAI Codex 辅助。
requirements: Requires the user’s extracted Xbox 360 dump: the original encrypted default.xex plus Content, System and the other dump folders. An ISO alone is not accepted, and the repository includes no game code, assets or generated translation output. The runtime decodes default.xex in memory and accepts only the approved original disc revision and Russian localization by SHA-256; title updates and other Xbox games need their own verified translation.

Playing the release needs 64-bit Windows 10/11 with a Direct3D 11 device. Source builds need Git, Visual Studio 2022 with ClangCL, CMake 3.24+, Python 3.11+, MSYS2 MinGW64 tools, standalone LLVM and about 15 GB. The build fetches hedge-dev/XenonRecomp at c5bfd90d and applies the bundled Darkness and correction patches before generating the translation.

The README reports full gameplay with mouse/controller input, XMA audio, saves, local achievements and added video and remapping menus; Xbox Live synchronization is unavailable. Under Proton in WSL2, the opening level rendered with audio, but camera movement and tutorial completion were not confirmed; Steam Deck remains unverified and there is no native Linux build.

The build runs a CTest suite of native and contract tests, and the updater re-tests builds and checks packaged files with SHA-256. These are project checks of the port, not proof of behavioral equivalence with the console release; this collection did not build or run it.

GPLv3 per COPYING, matching UnleashedRecomp/XenonRecomp; the generator patches are GPLv3, SMAA and the CC0 Xelu prompt icons keep their own terms, and the game retains separate rights. This is static recompilation, not recovered authored source. The README states that development includes OpenAI Codex assistance; no REA connection is established.

name: MarioKart 64: Recompiled — a native port through N64Recomp static recompilation
description_en: Statically recompiles the US Nintendo 64 release of Mario Kart 64 into a native Windows, Linux and macOS application with N64Recomp, rendering through RT64. The README distinguishes this from a source port: game code is translated from the user’s ROM, while headers and some functions from a decompilation fork support patches and enhancements. Enhancement, fidelity and input-lag claims are project-reported.
description_zh: 使用 N64Recomp 将北美版 Nintendo 64《马力欧卡丁车 64》静态重编译为 Windows、Linux 与 macOS 原生应用，并通过 RT64 渲染。README 将其与源码移植区分开：游戏代码由使用者提供的 ROM 转换而来，反编译分支中的头文件和部分函数用于实现补丁与增强。增强功能、还原度和输入延迟等说法均为项目自述。
requirements: Accepts only the user’s US N64 Mario Kart 64 ROM; other dump formats of that ROM are converted automatically, and the README states it is not an emulator for arbitrary ROMs. The repository and its releases contain no game assets. Source builds read the same US ROM as mk64.us.z64 plus a separate symbol-file submodule.

Running requires Direct3D 12.0 with Shader Model 6, Vulkan 1.2 or Metal Argument Buffers Tier 2; x86-64 CPUs need SSE4.1, and the README lists macOS 13.0+ on Apple Silicon or a 7th-generation Intel CPU. Known issues include Intel GPUs on Linux and the prebuilt Linux binary on some distributions.

Source builds need submodules, CMake 3.20+, C++20, and Clang/LLD with SDL2 and GTK 3 on Linux or Visual Studio 2022 with its Clang tools and make on Windows. N64Recomp and RSPRecomp are built separately and run on the provided TOML configurations to generate C code; patches compile against headers from a fork of the mk64 decompilation.

CI recompiles and builds Linux, Windows and macOS targets with a ROM held in a private repository behind CI secrets; it publishes no matching, fidelity or gameplay comparison. Release v0.9.2 (February 2026) offers Windows, Linux, Flatpak and macOS archives. Rendering-accuracy, framerate and input-lag statements are project claims; this collection did not build or run the port.

COPYING is GPL-3.0; original game content, decompilation-derived headers and libraries such as RT64 and RmlUi retain their own terms. Static recompilation translates machine code rather than recovering authored source; the reviewed files establish no AI or REA involvement, and no runtime reproduction is claimed.

name: Animal Crossing: matching GameCube decompilation
description_en: Reconstructs Animal Crossing’s GameCube code as C and C++ source that rebuilds the USA release’s main executable and its foresta.rel module. The dtk-template build reads the original binaries and assets from a user-supplied disc image, then checks both outputs against SHA-1 hashes. A separate native PC port builds on it; completeness figures remain project-reported here.
description_zh: 将 Animal Crossing 的 GameCube 代码重建为 C 与 C++ 源码，可重新构建美版的主可执行文件及 foresta.rel 模块。基于 dtk-template 的构建从使用者自备的光盘镜像读取原始二进制与素材，再用 SHA-1 哈希校验两个产物。另有原生 PC 移植以它为基础；此处的完成度数字仍为项目报告。
requirements: README lists one supported version, USA Rev 0 (GAFE01_00). configure.py also defines an Australia Rev 0 (GAFU01_00) target, but CI builds only the USA version and 19 objects are marked matching for USA alone. The outputs are a GameCube DOL and REL module, not a PC executable; the separate N64 Animal Forest decompilation the README links to is not covered here.

Requires the user’s own Animal Crossing (USA) disc image; README states the repository contains no game assets or assembly. The build configuration expects the disc’s main.dol to match a recorded SHA-1 before splitting it, so other revisions or modified images are not supported inputs.

Windows builds use native Python and ninja; macOS adds wine-crossover, and Linux uses an automatically downloaded wibo wrapper on x86 or Wine elsewhere. configure.py downloads pinned decomp-toolkit, binutils, Metrowerks CodeWarrior GameCube compiler, objdiff and sjiswrap releases; objdiff supports per-object diffing.

The default ninja target runs decomp-toolkit’s SHA-1 check of static.dol and foresta.rel against build.sha1. configure.py lists 4,005 objects as matching and none as non-matching, and CI builds with a private container that supplies the original files. The mutable decomp.dev page reports 100.00% decompiled and fully linked at this commit; this review did not rerun the build or checks.

The repository is dedicated under CC0 1.0. Original game content and the downloaded toolchain binaries are outside that dedication and keep their own rights. The reviewed sources establish no AI or REA attribution, and no runtime reproduction is claimed.

name: Kingdom Hearts 358/2 Days: a matching Nintendo DS decompilation
description_en: Reconstructs the ARM9 program and overlays of the EU Nintendo DS release of Kingdom Hearts 358/2 Days as C that recompiles byte for byte with CodeWarrior. README reports all 306 modules byte-identical, with about 99.5% of functions in real C and library assembly counted separately; the ARM7 binary is outside its scope. The repository holds no ROM, game assets or extracted disassembly and produces no playable build.
description_zh: 将 Nintendo DS 欧版《王国之心 358/2 Days》的 ARM9 程序及覆盖模块重建为 C 源码，以 CodeWarrior 重新编译后逐字节一致。README 报告全部 306 个模块字节一致，约 99.5% 的函数为真正的 C，库自身的汇编另行统计；ARM7 二进制不在范围内。仓库不含 ROM、游戏素材或提取的反汇编，也不生成可玩版本。
requirements: README reports every function of the EU (YKGP) ARM9 program and its overlays matched and all initialized data reconstructed, with 306 of 306 rebuilt modules byte-identical; the remaining work is readability, such as shared structures, naming and file grouping. It counts 23,125 of about 23,233 functions as real C and tracks 108 assembly implementations (library routines and two game functions that need clz) separately. docs/ARM7.md states that the decomp covers the ARM9 only. This is a matching decompilation, not a port, and it produces no playable build or redistributable binary.

Requires the user’s own EU ROM dump, days.nds: 268,435,456 bytes, SHA-1 6fae8f5bbe80114b4e2535260eab5f4d0fc8a844 (CONTRIBUTING.md also lists SHA-256 and MD5). Other dumps will not line up with the committed addresses. The repository tracks no ROM, extracted data (including the extracted asm/ tree), build output or proprietary toolchain, and a pull-request check rejects added ROM, binary or asset files.

CONTRIBUTING.md lists Python 3 with capstone, pyelftools and ndspy, the dsd extraction and delinking tool, the proprietary CodeWarrior mwccarm 3.0 build 139 compiler (not supplied), arm-none-eabi-as and a Ninja-driven mwccarm/mwldarm build; its commands call tools/dsd.exe alongside Bash scripts. A few precompiled-middleware units use an older mwccarm through per-file compiler overrides.

dsd check modules compares each built module with the base ROM, verify_idx.py checks single functions including relocations, and the ROM round-trip script is expected to differ from the reference dump only in four non-functional CRC bytes. CONTRIBUTING notes that functions listed as known mismatches are kept out of the link and filled with original bytes. CI does not build the game; it rejects forbidden files and regenerates progress reports. decomp.dev reports YKGP 100.00% decompiled and fully linked at the reviewed commit, counting verified SDK assembly; this collection did not rerun these checks.

Contributors’ decompilation and tooling are dedicated to the public domain under CC0 1.0; the original game and its assets remain their owners’ property, and the CodeWarrior compiler is not distributed. DS Protect sources are reconstructed after taxicat1/dsprot, and the SDK identification harness compiles NitroSDK sources from pret/pokediamond. The reviewed sources disclose no REA or AI use, and no runtime reproduction is claimed; the separate khdays-port PC runtime is not covered.

name: rtl_433
description_en: Receives and decodes transmissions from ISM-band devices such as weather sensors, remote controls, doorbells and alarm sensors, using RTL-SDR or SoapySDR receivers or recorded I/Q files, and emits decoded fields as JSON, CSV, MQTT and other outputs. For signals no built-in decoder recognizes, a pulse analyzer reports OOK/FSK timings and hints for a flexible -X decoder that slices frames into bits; its analysis guide leaves mapping those bits to values to the analyst, working from known readings.
description_zh: 接收并解码 ISM 频段设备（如气象传感器、遥控器、门铃和报警传感器）的无线传输，可使用 RTL-SDR 或 SoapySDR 接收机，也可读取录制的 I/Q 文件，并以 JSON、CSV、MQTT 等格式输出解码字段。对内置解码器无法识别的信号，脉冲分析器会报告 OOK/FSK 时序，并给出灵活 -X 解码器的提示，用于将帧切分为比特；按其分析指南，把这些比特对应到具体数值仍需分析者依据已知读数完成。
requirements: Live reception needs an RTL2832-based RTL-SDR dongle or a SoapySDR device; the README names LimeSDR, PlutoSDR, HackRF One and SoapyRemote among actively tested devices, and rtl_tcp servers are accepted. Without a receiver, it reads recorded CU8, CS16 or CF32 I/Q and AM sample files, and -S saves captured signals as files.

Written in portable C99 and built with CMake; RTL-SDR and SoapySDR libraries are optional at build time, and OpenSSL is needed only for TLS outputs. Packages exist for Debian/Ubuntu (rtl-433), FreeBSD and Homebrew; release 25.12 (2025-12-12) ships Linux, macOS arm64 and Windows binaries, and the reviewed master commit is dated 2026-10-11.

At review the README listed 380 device protocols numbered up to 386, 44 of them disabled by default and enabled with -R or a configuration file. Built-in decoders cover those listed models only; for other signals the analyzer and flex decoders frame OOK/FSK pulses and slice them into bits, and do not infer field meanings or protocol semantics.
GPL-2.0. The optional HTTP API output listens on 0.0.0.0:8433 by default. No capture, decoding or analysis was run, and no device compatibility is implied.

name: decomp.me
description_en: Collaborative decompilation website for matching work: its compile service builds candidate source with a selected platform compiler, assembles the target assembly and diffs the two objects with asm-differ. m2c drafts initial decompilations for its MIPS, PowerPC, ARM and SuperH platforms. The 18 platform definitions span N64, PlayStation, PS2, PSP, GameCube/Wii, Wii U, DS, GBA, 3DS, Switch, Saturn, Dreamcast and Xbox 360 plus IRIX, Mac OS X, MS-DOS, Win32 and Android x86.
description_zh: 面向匹配反编译的协作网站：其编译服务用选定平台的编译器编译候选源码，汇编目标汇编代码，并用 asm-differ 对比两个目标文件。对其 MIPS、PowerPC、ARM 和 SuperH 平台，m2c 可生成初步反编译代码。18 个平台定义涵盖 N64、PlayStation、PS2、PSP、GameCube/Wii、Wii U、DS、GBA、3DS、Switch、Saturn、Dreamcast 和 Xbox 360，以及 IRIX、Mac OS X、MS-DOS、Win32 和 Android x86。
requirements: Use the hosted site or self-host the Next.js/Django stack with Docker and Docker Compose; the self-hosting guide asks for at least 4 GB RAM, ideally 6 GB+. Its Docker configuration disables Switch support by default because of the Clang compilers' size, and ENABLE_<PLATFORM>_SUPPORT variables enable platforms. The live site answered automated requests with a browser check, so its pages, accounts and available compilers were not reviewed.

Each platform definition names its assembler, objdump and nm commands; compilers are added as packages in the separate decompme/compilers repository, which was not reviewed. Compiler, assembler and objdump subprocesses can run in an nsjail sandbox, enabled by default in the cromper container; outside it, nsjail must be built locally with unprivileged user namespaces enabled.

MIT license; the README notes that dependencies keep their own licenses, and this entry makes no claim about compiler licensing. No tagged releases, so this entry pins the reviewed main-branch commit. Diffs show instruction-level differences for the compiled code and m2c output is a draft; neither recovers names, types or semantics. No code was compiled and no instance was run.

name: TonyWasAProSkater: a THPS1 native port forked from a matching decompilation
description_en: Ports Tony Hawk’s Pro Skater (PlayStation, USA) to native Windows and Linux builds from a fork of an in-progress matching decompilation of the retail executable. The decompilation recompiles reconstructed functions with a Psy-Q toolchain and compares them byte for byte with the user’s retail executable, while the port replaces PlayStation hardware and libraries with SDL2 and OpenGL services. Play needs the user’s own disc image; matching and gameplay results remain project-reported.
description_zh: 从一个仍在进行中的零售版可执行文件一致性反编译项目派生分支，将 Tony Hawk’s Pro Skater（PlayStation 美版）移植为原生 Windows 与 Linux 程序。反编译部分用 Psy-Q 工具链重新编译已重建的函数，并与使用者自备的零售可执行文件逐字节比对；移植部分则以 SDL2 和 OpenGL 服务取代 PlayStation 硬件和库。运行需使用者自备光盘镜像；一致性与可玩性结果仍为项目报告。
requirements: The reviewed main branch, a fork of LANCommander/THPS, targets only the retail PS1 USA executable SLUS_008.60, not later games in the series. decomp/PROGRESS.md, generated 2026-10-13, reports 88.0% of game-code bytes (928 of 1,178 functions) byte-exact, with the Psy-Q libraries out of scope. The port compiles a separate fork of that code in game/; decomp/ stays the byte-matching reference and is not built into the port, so the playable executable is not itself a matching build.

Play requires a raw MODE2/2352 BIN image of the user’s own Tony Hawk’s Pro Skater (USA) PlayStation disc; the Dreamcast disc image (.gdi and its tracks) can supply the assets instead. The first start copies about 630 MB into a Data folder. Building also needs the retail SLUS_008.60 executable from the user’s disc for the function layout. README states that no game assets or original executable are committed, while decompiled code and initialised data are included.

Builds run on Windows with MSYS2’s 32-bit MinGW toolchain and SDL2 (64-bit builds use ucrt64) or on x86 Linux with multilib GCC and 32-bit SDL2, plus Python 3 and Ghidra’s GNU demangler; a Psy-Q library name table is generated from ghidra_psx_ldr signatures. Running needs 64-bit Windows 10/11 or x86 Linux with 32-bit SDL2 and OpenGL libraries, and an OpenGL 3.3 GPU. Re-verifying matched functions additionally needs Node and the Psy-Q 4.5 compiler, which is not distributed.

decomp/tools/check_all.mjs recompiles every function in matched.tsv and compares it with the retail bytes; C that replaces hand-written assembly and Sony libraries is checked by replaying recorded game states against the original MIPS code. Port changes are checked with deterministic runs whose frames and saves are compared with an earlier build. README reports all nine career levels playable and an approximate rather than exact PS1 reverb; this collection did not rerun these checks.

README and the port README describe the project’s own code as MIT under a repository LICENSE, but the reviewed tree has no LICENSE file and GitHub detects none. The port README states that decompiled game code, data and all assets remain © Activision/Neversoft; linked libraries such as SDL 2, PL_MPEG and glad keep their own terms. The tree includes CLAUDE.md project notes and a GhidraMCP configuration, but the README states no AI or REA use, so none is recorded.

name: P.T. for PC: a behavior-based engine reimplementation that reads the PS4 data
description_en: Reimplements P.T.’s game logic in C++ on a new Vulkan engine that reads levels, models, textures, sounds, scripts and cutscenes from the user’s own PS4 copy at run time. The author documents reverse-engineered file formats and used the shadPS4 emulator as a behavior and frame reference. Fidelity to the original is author-reported, and the use of AI coding tools is disclosed.
description_zh: 在新的 Vulkan 引擎上用 C++ 重新实现 P.T. 的游戏逻辑，运行时从使用者自有的 PS4 版本读取关卡、模型、贴图、声音、脚本和过场动画。作者记录了逆向得出的文件格式，并以 shadPS4 模拟器作为行为与画面的对照参考。与原作的一致程度为作者报告，项目也披露使用了 AI 编程工具。
requirements: Requires the user’s own copy of P.T.: the port is built and tested with the US release CUSA01127, as a console dump folder or a fake PKG made from it; the EU and Japanese releases install with a note but the author has not seen their data. Store PKGs are encrypted for their console and are not decrypted. The installer copies only chunk1.psarc, texture.qar and pathid_list_ps4.bin, and no game data is in the repository or installer.

Runs on Windows 10/11 x64, Linux x86-64 with glibc 2.38+, or macOS 14+, with a Vulkan 1.3 GPU (MoltenVK on macOS). Building needs CMake and Ninja, plus Visual Studio 2022 Build Tools, clang-cl and the Vulkan SDK on Windows, or GCC 13/clang 17 with glslc on Linux; CMake fetches SDL3, Lua 5.1, whisper.cpp and other dependencies and checks downloaded models and SDKs by SHA-256. One section needs a microphone or a configured substitute key.

This is an engine reimplementation, not an emulator, decompilation or static recompilation: the README says the logic was rebuilt from the original’s behavior. It reports the whole teaser as playable, including the voice section, and adds optional upscalers, ray-traced effects, photo mode, a museum, mods, extra languages and experimental VR and third-person views. VR has run only against a simulated runtime, the Intel Mac build has not been run, and the tree contains unreleased 1.0.2 changes.

Verification is author-run: CMake unit-test targets, a windowless walkthrough script that plays scripted routes and checks the log, and frame comparisons against shadPS4. This collection did not build or run the port, and those checks do not establish equivalence with the PS4 release.

MIT covers the port’s own code; the bundled Noto fonts (OFL), the LGPL LibOrbisPkg installer helper and other dependencies keep their own licenses, and P.T. content belongs to Konami. The README discloses AI coding tools in development and debugging; no REA connection is established.

name: SpaghettiKart: a native Mario Kart 64 port built on decompiled source
description_en: Builds a native Mario Kart 64 port for Windows, Linux, macOS and Switch from source that keeps the Mario Kart 64 decompilation’s file layout, running on libultraship’s reimplemented N64 SDK. Its bundled Torch extractor converts the user’s US ROM into an asset archive, and the port adds mods, custom tracks and an editor. The README does not name its upstream decompilation, and no matching or fidelity checks are published.
description_zh: 基于沿用《马力欧卡丁车 64》反编译项目文件结构的源码，构建适用于 Windows、Linux、macOS 和 Switch 的原生移植，运行在 libultraship 重新实现的 N64 SDK 之上。随附的 Torch 提取器将使用者自备的美版 ROM 转换为素材归档，移植还增加了模组、自定义赛道和编辑器。README 未写明其上游反编译项目，也未发布一致性或还原度检查。
requirements: The README does not name its upstream, but the tree keeps the Mario Kart 64 decompilation’s src/, course, extraction and progress-tooling layout, while new engine and port directories add C++ systems, mod loading, custom tracks and the unfinished HM64 Labs editor. Release 1.0.0 “Bolognese Alfa” (February 2026) is the latest stable release; nightly CI builds are for playtesting only.

Supports only the US ROM with SHA-1 579C48E211AE952530FFC8738709F078D5DD215E in .z64 byte order. The bundled extractor converts that user-supplied ROM into mk64.o2r; the README states that SpaghettiKart includes no copyrighted assets, and the Switch build reuses an archive generated by a PC release.

Source builds need submodules (libultraship, Torch, fast64 and others), CMake 3.16+ and Python 3. Windows uses Visual Studio 2022 with the v143 toolset and at least 8 GB of RAM; Linux needs GCC or Clang with SDL2, libzip, tinyxml2, spdlog, Boost and Ogg/Vorbis packages. Rendering backends are DirectX 11 on Windows, OpenGL on all platforms and Metal on macOS.
