The public site is a Cloudflare Pages deployment from main, and self-hosting the release archive needs the same isolation headers.

WEB_ARCHITECTURE.md records author-run checks with user-selected retail files: a complete Lunatic Final-B route in Chromium and on an earlier Firefox bridge, a Stage 6B practice run, persistence tests showing no DAT in IndexedDB, and replay-driven pacing samples near 60 Hz under the SwiftShader and llvmpipe software renderers. These are bounded correctness observations, not hardware benchmarks or binary comparisons; this collection ran nothing.

MIT covers repository code and documentation, not the original game, DAT files, music or graphics; the pinned Detours submodule keeps its own terms. README describes this repository as the web-focused fork of N0zoM1z0/th08 with its history retained. The reviewed web-port sources establish no REA attribution, and no runtime reproduction is claimed.

name: ipsw
description_en: Command-line toolkit for Apple firmware research and reverse engineering. It downloads and unpacks IPSWs, OTAs and KDKs and compares builds; inspects Mach-O load commands, symbols, signatures and entitlements with ARM64 disassembly; finds symbols and cross-references in dyld shared caches, extracts dylibs and dumps Objective-C headers and Swift metadata; extracts KEXTs and compares kernelcaches; and parses IMG4, decrypts AEA archives and inspects iBoot and coprocessor firmware.
description_zh: 面向 Apple 固件研究与逆向工程的命令行工具包。可下载并解包 IPSW、OTA 和 KDK 并比较不同构建；检查 Mach-O 的加载命令、符号、签名和权限，并反汇编 ARM64 代码；在 dyld 共享缓存中查找符号和交叉引用、提取 dylib、导出 Objective-C 头文件并查看 Swift 元数据；提取 KEXT 并比较 kernelcache；还能解析 IMG4、解密 AEA 归档，以及检查 iBoot 和协处理器固件。
requirements: Release at review: v3.1.739, published 2026-10-16, with Linux, macOS, Windows and iOS builds plus deb, rpm, apk and Arch packages; the reviewed master commit is three cache and documentation commits ahead. Install with Homebrew (tap or core formula), snap or Scoop. The extras build (Unicorn-based dyld emulation, libusb device commands) and the Frida build are macOS only. Source builds need a C toolchain for CGO and, per the README, Go 1.26+, although go.mod declares go 1.27.

Firmware, caches and binaries are supplied by the user or fetched with the download commands. The README's device and App Store Connect commands are outside this entry's reverse-engineering scope. With --dec, macho disass and dyld disass send disassembly to the LLM provider chosen with --dec-llm: hosted OpenAI-compatible, Anthropic, Gemini or router APIs, ACP agent CLIs, or local Ollama. The separate ipswd daemon exposes a REST API, and the README points agents to the separate ipsw-skill repository, which was not reviewed.

MIT license. The README notes that extracted dylibs can still reference metadata elsewhere in the cache, so it recommends Objective-C analysis on the cache itself. LLM decompilation output is model-generated and needs verification. No firmware was downloaded or analyzed.

name: OpenXcom: an open-source clone of X-COM: UFO Defense and Terror from the Deep
description_en: Reimplements MicroProse’s UFO: Enemy Unknown (X-COM: UFO Defense) and X-COM: Terror from the Deep as a C++/SDL engine that runs on the user’s original game resources. Game data such as items, craft, research and missions is expressed in YAML rulesets, which also carry its standard mods and a wider modding ecosystem. It is a clone that reuses original content, not recovered MicroProse code.
description_zh: 以 C++/SDL 引擎重新实现 MicroProse 的 UFO: Enemy Unknown（X-COM: UFO Defense）与 X-COM: Terror from the Deep，并在使用者自己的原游戏资源上运行。物品、飞行器、研究和任务等游戏数据以 YAML 规则集表达，这些规则集也承载其标准模组及更广泛的模组生态。这是复用原内容的克隆实现，而非恢复出的 MicroProse 代码。
requirements: The reviewed master snapshot reports version 1.0 Dev; the last tagged release is v1.0 from 2014, and a nightly workflow builds later Windows, Linux and macOS versions. It covers both games and can import saved games from the originals, while standard mods based on XcomUtil and UFOExtender add optional changes. The reviewed sources do not describe how original behaviour was determined.

Requires an unmodified copy of the resources from either or both original games. For UFO these include the GEODATA, GEOGRAPH, MAPS, ROUTES, SOUND, TERRAIN, UFOGRAPH and UNITS folders, and TFTD needs a similar set. The README warns against modded copies such as XcomUtil-patched data; the Windows installer can detect Steam editions.

Building targets C++11 with CMake 3.5+, Visual C++, Xcode or a plain Makefile, against SDL 1.2, SDL_mixer, SDL_gfx 2.0.22+, SDL_image and yaml-cpp 0.5.3+. CI compiles debug builds on Linux, 32-bit Windows and macOS.

CI only compiles the code, and the repository has no automated behaviour tests, so fidelity to the original games is not demonstrated by published checks. This review did not build or run the project.

Source headers apply GPL-3.0-or-later, and the README notes modified SDL_gfx code (LGPL) used with its author’s permission. Original game resources keep their own rights. The reviewed sources establish no REA or AI use.

name: Skate 3 Recomp: a native Xbox 360 recompilation through ReXGlue
description_en: Recompiles the Xbox 360 version of Skate 3 into native Windows, Linux and macOS builds with a Skate-specific fork of the ReXGlue SDK. Since v2.0.0 a native Direct3D 12 and Vulkan renderer with ports of the game’s own material shading replaces emulation of the Xbox 360 GPU, which remains as a fallback. Game files come from the user’s disc image; the author calls the native renderer early and has not tested the game end to end.
description_zh: 借助 ReXGlue SDK 的 Skate 专用分支，将 Xbox 360 版《Skate 3》重编译为 Windows、Linux 与 macOS 原生版本。自 v2.0.0 起，基于 Direct3D 12 和 Vulkan、移植了游戏自身材质着色的原生渲染器取代对 Xbox 360 GPU 的模拟，模拟渲染器保留为后备。游戏文件来自使用者的光盘镜像；作者称原生渲染器尚处早期，且尚未完整测试整个游戏。
requirements: The latest reviewed release is v2.0.2 (July 2026) for Windows, Linux and experimental Apple-silicon macOS; the README calls Windows the most tested platform. Known native-renderer issues include streaming pop-in, skater-customization rendering, Hall of Meat highlights and skate-park parity; frame-rate and power gains over the emulated renderer are author-reported.

Players choose an ISO of their own Xbox 360 copy of Skate 3 for the built-in installer, and DLC needs the user’s own package files. Source codegen reads default.xex and data/webkit/EAWebkit.xex from an extracted dump and should also be given the Title Update 3 package, whose patched executables release builds require. Retail files and generated recompilation sources are git-ignored.

Builds need CMake 3.25+, Ninja and Clang 18 or newer (Clang 20 is recommended on Ubuntu 24.04); MSVC and Apple Clang are unsupported. The pinned rexglue-sdk submodule is the author’s fork on the rexglue 0.8.0 line, holding the runtime, codegen, input, timing and both graphics backends. Vulkan SPIR-V shader binaries are committed, and macOS uses Homebrew LLVM with MoltenVK.

The reviewed tree contains no CI workflow, test suite or fidelity comparison, and the README says the game has not been played through on the native renderer. Visual-parity statements are project claims; this collection did not build or run the port.

Neither the repository nor its GitHub metadata declares a license for the project’s code; the rexglue fork carries a Xenia-derived BSD-3-Clause notice, and Skate 3 content retains Electronic Arts’ rights. The reviewed sources establish no AI or REA involvement, and no runtime reproduction is claimed.

name: decomp.wtf
description_en: A discontinued local app and MCP server that hands AI coding agents one function of a user-owned console game at a time, compiles each C attempt with the game’s period compiler and accepts it only when the linked result matches the original bytes. It can start a project from a ROM or disc image, or work inside forks of public decompilation projects listed on decomp.dev, where objdiff judges the result. Its final commit, dated 15 October 2026, marks it discontinued in response to opposition in the decompilation community; the code stays under MIT without further fixes or releases.
description_zh: 一款已停止开发的本地应用与 MCP 服务，把用户自有主机游戏的函数逐个交给 AI 编程智能体，用该游戏当年的编译器编译每次提交的 C 代码，只有链接后的结果与原始字节一致才算通过。它可从 ROM 或光盘镜像新建项目，也可在 decomp.dev 所列公开反编译项目的分叉中工作，由 objdiff 判定结果。其 2026 年 10 月 15 日的最后一次提交宣布停止开发，理由是反编译社区的反对；代码仍以 MIT 许可保留，但不再修复或发布新版本。
requirements: The reviewed pin is the discontinuation commit of the archived repository, at package version 0.10.6, which the README names as the last installable release. The author will not fix issues, review pull requests or publish releases; existing installs keep working without updates. It runs on Linux and, marked unstable, on Windows inside its own WSL 2 distribution; macOS is unsupported. It needs Python 3.12 or later, and its installer sets up uv, the app, pinned checksum-verified period compilers and the m2c draft decompiler.

Agents connect through the local decomp mcp server or a Claude Code plugin that adds a decompile skill. README lists Claude Code, Codex CLI, Antigravity CLI, opencode, other MCP clients and a built-in loop for OpenAI-compatible APIs, including local models. Agents receive only decomp.wtf’s tools, without a shell. Users pay their own model provider; the author reports about 8 cents for a small function with Claude Code and warns that large functions take many more attempts.

Users supply their own ROM, disc image or program file. The tool contains no game code or ROMs apart from a bundled demo N64 ROM built from public-domain code and zlib. Proprietary period compilers such as IDO and CodeWarrior are installed only after the user agrees. Continuing a public decomp clones that project locally and runs its build scripts, so the README advises forking only trusted projects.

README lists GameCube, Wii and N64 as recommended and PlayStation, PlayStation 2, Game Boy Advance and DS as beta, tested mostly on homemade games. It reports imports tested on named commercial titles and exports that rebuild the input byte for byte, with GameCube and Wii files linked and checksum-checked in dtk-template projects. These remain author statements: the repository has a pytest suite but no CI workflow at the pin, publishes no game results, and this collection ran nothing.

The repository is MIT-licensed. Its README asks users to work only on games they own, not to circumvent copy protection, not to publish decompiled code of games whose rights they do not hold, and to follow each public project’s contribution rules, noting that many community decomps reject AI-written contributions. Nothing is sent upstream automatically. The project disclaims affiliation with the tools it builds on, and the reviewed sources establish no REA connection.

name: Uncharted: The Nathan Drake Collection native Windows port
description_en: Runs the PS4 Uncharted: The Nathan Drake Collection’s own x86-64 executables natively on Windows: a runtime supplies the PS4 system libraries and a shadPS4-derived Vulkan renderer executes the GPU work. The port adds a per-game launcher, resolution patches and modern upscaling, and its status table reports all three games playable with listed open issues. It is a compatibility-runtime port rather than a decompilation, and its results remain project-reported.
description_zh: 在 Windows 上原生运行 PS4 版《神秘海域：内森·德雷克合集》自身的 x86-64 可执行文件：由运行时提供 PS4 系统库，并以源自 shadPS4 的 Vulkan 渲染器执行 GPU 工作。该移植提供按游戏保存设置的启动器、分辨率补丁与现代超分辨率技术，其状态表报告三部游戏均可游玩，并列出未解决问题。这是兼容运行时移植而非反编译重建，结果仍为项目报告。
requirements: Reviewed at the commit of release v0.2.3 (2026-10-18); v0.1.0 was published on 2026-10-15. README reports Drake’s Fortune, Among Thieves and Drake’s Deception playable, with the Collection menu, game switching, saves, audio, movies and controllers working. Known issues include a Drake’s Fortune grenade-launcher fault, cropped ultrawide views, single-core GPU-command limits on slower CPUs, experimental multithreaded rendering and less play-testing for Uncharted 3. The original game code is run with local patches, not rebuilt from recovered source.

Supply your own dumped copy of the PS4 game CUSA02344, the folder holding eboot.bin and sce_sys; game update 1.02 is optional and recommended. README says no game files are in the repository or its builds, and the preparation script patches the game executables locally for resolution and update handling. The project disclaims affiliation with Sony, Naughty Dog and Bluepoint Games, and the games keep their own rights.

Play needs 64-bit Windows 10 or 11, a CPU with AVX, F16C, BMI1, MOVBE and LZCNT (Intel Haswell or newer, or any AMD Ryzen), a Vulkan 1.3 GPU and about 6 GB of free RAM, with 16 GB recommended. Local builds use an MSYS2 CLANG64 toolchain with CMake, Ninja, the Vulkan stack, SDL3, FFmpeg, Boost and other listed packages, plus a Windows Python 3.10+ with Pillow for packaging. GitHub Actions builds the Windows package on each push, and the launcher’s updater checks release SHA-256 digests.

Evidence is play-testing and diagnostics: STATUS.md records native runtime tests for fibers, services, video decoding, buffered input and clock timing, with the cause and user confirmation of individual fixes. README frame rates come from the author’s RTX 5080 and integrated Radeon tests plus one player report. The CI workflow builds and publishes packages without automated game tests. This collection read the sources without running the port or any game.

README declares GPL v2 or later. The runtime started from FelipePrado0’s GPL-2.0 gow3_pc and the shadPS4 video core, and the TAA camera approach credits SuperMedo’s GPL v2 Uncharted port. Packages bundle third-party libraries; NVIDIA’s DLSS DLL, fetched by a build script from NVIDIA’s DLSS repository, stays under NVIDIA’s license. STATUS.md mentions REA only as unable to decompile the prepared ELF on Windows and names no AI model; the post’s Claude attribution comes from a third-party account, so no AI or REA workflow is established.

name: TH095: function-level reconstruction of Shoot the Bullet 1.02a
description_en: Reconstructs source for the original Japanese Touhou 9.5: Shoot the Bullet 1.02a executable, accepting function exactness only through reproducible byte comparison of pinned Visual C++ .NET 2003 builds against one hash-attested target. The whole program also compiles and links into a playable Windows i386 executable, while README keeps playability, function matching and whole-executable identity as separate statuses.
description_zh: 为日版 Touhou 9.5：东方文花帖 1.02a 原可执行文件重建源码；只有使用固定版本 Visual C++ .NET 2003 构建、并与单一经哈希核验的目标进行可复现字节比较后，才认定函数级一致。整个程序也能编译链接为可游玩的 Windows i386 可执行文件，而 README 将可玩性、函数匹配与整个可执行文件一致性列为相互独立的状态。
requirements: Generated PROGRESS.md reports 697 confirmed authored functions among 1,880 candidates, all with source, and 696 canonically exact, covering 99.22% of confirmed authored bytes; Controller::GetInput keeps one differing byte. README does not claim whole-executable byte identity, lists semantic reconstruction as active and Windows x86-64, Linux and Web ports as planned, and tags the playable baseline v0.1.0-windows-i386 without release binaries.

Supply your own original Japanese 1.02a th095.exe matching the size, SHA-256 and MD5 in README, imported as resources/th095.exe; playing also needs the game’s data. README says copyrighted executables, game data and private analysis databases are not included, and public CI runs only target-independent checks.

scripts/bootstrap-tools.sh needs curl, git, sha256sum, tar, unzip, uv and Wine, then fetches checksum-pinned Ghidra 12.1.3, Temurin JDK 21, objdiff 3.8.0 and Microsoft Visual C++ .NET 2003 (13.10.3077) binaries from a third-party archive repository; reccmp 0.1.6 is also pinned. scripts/build-whole.py cold-compiles and links the production graph and refuses stubbed or force-linked images.

Exact credit requires a zero-difference COFF function comparison recorded in the match ledgers; Ghidra, IDA MCP and runtime observation count only as supporting evidence. README cites a full-game runtime video using a test-only no-death launcher plus separate normal-build tests, and RUNTIME_ISSUES.md notes those checks used 2026-09-10 source, with later semantic changes only compile- and link-validated. This collection ran nothing.

MIT covers repository code and documentation, not the game or its assets; the downloaded compiler and tools keep their own terms. The repository carries coding-agent rules and skills and a GPT web Ghidra bridge but does not itself document REA use; REA’s separately published Touhou essay discusses this project. No runtime reproduction is claimed here.

name: DynamoRIO
description_en: Runtime code manipulation system for building dynamic tools that observe or transform any part of an unmodified program while it runs. Its API and IA-32/AMD64/ARM/AArch64 instruction manipulation library allow arbitrary changes to application instructions, not only inserted callouts. The release package bundles tools including drcov for code coverage, drltrace for library-call tracing, drstrace for Windows system calls, drmemtrace instruction and memory traces and the drdisas disassembler. It is a framework for building instrumentation tools, distinct from Frida's scripting of live processes.
description_zh: 运行时代码操作系统，用于构建在未修改程序运行期间观察或变换其任意部分的动态工具。其 API 与 IA-32/AMD64/ARM/AArch64 指令操作库允许任意修改应用指令，而不仅限于插入回调。发布包附带 drcov 代码覆盖率、drltrace 库调用跟踪、drstrace Windows 系统调用跟踪、drmemtrace 指令与内存访问跟踪以及 drdisas 反汇编器等工具。它是用于构建插桩工具的框架，与 Frida 对运行中进程编写脚本的方式不同。
requirements: The README lists Windows, Linux and Android on IA-32, AMD64, ARM and AArch64 hardware; macOS support is in progress. Latest stable release at review: release_11.3.0-1, published 2025-01-11, with Windows, Linux, AArch64 Linux, ARM Linux EABIHF and ARM Android packages. Weekly cronbuild packages follow master (cronbuild-11.91.20741, published 2026-10-17, with no Android package); this entry pins the reviewed master commit.

Custom tools are written against the API, whose documentation ships in the release package and online; API samples cover memory-address, instruction and basic-block tracing and instruction counting. The README names WinAFL, the Arm Instruction Emulator, DrCCTProf, VClinic and GWPSan as external tools built on it and bundles Dr. Memory; none is catalogued separately here.

Primarily BSD. The drsyscall, drwrap and drutil extensions and the Dr. Memory Framework libraries are LGPL 2.1, and the drsyms extension links elfutils libraries under LGPL 3. The README's efficiency and transparency statements were not tested; no programs were instrumented.

name: LGwebOS-menubar: a native macOS remote for LG webOS TVs
description_en: A native macOS menu-bar app that pairs with an LG webOS TV over its local encrypted WebSocket interface to launch apps, switch inputs, adjust volume and picture settings, send pointer input and cast selected media. The project credits the public Connect SDK for webOS protocol behavior and reuses PyWebOSTV’s registration manifest. Testing covers one TV on webOS 5.0.
description_zh: 一款原生 macOS 菜单栏应用，通过 LG webOS 电视在局域网内的加密 WebSocket 接口完成配对，可启动应用、切换输入源、调节音量和画面设置、发送指针输入并投放所选媒体。项目称 webOS 协议行为参考了公开的 Connect SDK，并沿用 PyWebOSTV 的注册清单。测试仅覆盖一台 webOS 5.0 电视。
requirements: Reviewed at the 2026-10-13 head. It needs macOS 14 or later, Xcode Command Line Tools with Swift 5.9 or later, and an LG webOS TV on the same network; the only tested set is an LG 50UN7310PSC on webOS 5.0, and other models and versions are unverified. Pairing must be accepted on the TV, an IPv4 address is required, and Wake-on-LAN needs the TV’s MAC address.

scripts/build.sh produces a locally signed, unnotarized app bundle. Pairing uses encrypted WebSockets on port 3001; the app pins the TV certificate after explicit approval and keeps pairing keys in Keychain. The repository ships no device addresses or pairing keys, and a privacy-check script scans files before publishing.

The offline --self-check runs preference, certificate, pointer, Home, usage, resource and loopback media tests without a TV. These are implementation checks, not conformance tests against LG’s interface, and this review ran neither them nor a TV.

The README narrows the author’s post: screen time is counted locally only while the app is connected, AirPlay support is limited to guidance for macOS Screen Mirroring, picture-setting changes depend on TV permissions, and casting depends on the TV’s codecs and DLNA service.

MIT covers the project code; the PyWebOSTV manifest keeps its MIT notice, and LG, app and console icons keep their owners’ rights. Commits credit Claude as co-author, and an X post by the same account credits REA, but the repository does not mention REA, so REA use is unconfirmed. This is an unofficial client, not recovered LG software.

name: PS2Recomp
description_en: Experimental static recompiler that translates MIPS R5900 code from PlayStation 2 ELF executables into C++ and links it with a bundled runtime. ps2xAnalyzer or a Ghidra export script produces a per-game TOML of functions, stubs, skips and instruction patches; ps2xRecomp emits a literal instruction-by-instruction translation; ps2xRuntime and ps2xIOP supply guest memory, syscall dispatch, IOP module execution with HLE fallbacks and partial, largely stubbed GS/VU hardware. Output is not decompiled source, and getting a game to run remains per-game porting work.
description_zh: 实验性的静态重编译器，将 PlayStation 2 ELF 可执行文件中的 MIPS R5900 代码转换为 C++，并与随附的运行时链接。ps2xAnalyzer 或 Ghidra 导出脚本为每款游戏生成包含函数、存根、跳过项和指令补丁的 TOML 配置；ps2xRecomp 输出逐条指令的直译代码；ps2xRuntime 与 ps2xIOP 提供客户机内存、系统调用分发、带 HLE 回退的 IOP 模块执行，以及仅部分实现、大多为存根的 GS/VU 硬件。输出不是反编译源码，让游戏真正运行仍需针对每款游戏进行移植。
requirements: Building needs CMake 3.20+ and a C++20 compiler; the README says it is tested mainly with MSVC, and some vector paths need SSE4/AVX host support. CMake fetches ELFIO, toml11, fmt, libdwarf and raylib at configure time, plus Dear ImGui when the debug UI is enabled. GitHub lists five source-only prereleases, v0.0 to v0.4 (the latest from 2026-04-05), with no binaries attached; the reviewed main commit (2026-10-14) is 36 commits after v0.4.

The user supplies the game ELF; the project ships no game code, and its project-description guidance names the original release as one the user must own. The preferred workflow exports functions from Ghidra with the bundled ExportPS2Functions.java script, while ps2_analyzer suits ELFs with debug symbols. Stub address bindings and game overrides target one exact ELF build and are not portable across games, regions or builds.

The README lists very poor VU and GS performance and partial, often stubbed hardware emulation as limitations. No game compatibility or finished port is implied; downstream ports built with it need separate review. The tree also holds Android and PS Vita build directories and a ps2xStudio front end, which were not reviewed.
GPL-3.0; fetched dependencies keep their own licenses, and the README cites PCSX2 as a runtime reference. No recompilation, build or game was run.

name: CorsixTH: an open reimplementation of Theme Hospital
description_en: Reimplements the engine of Bullfrog’s 1997 Theme Hospital, with game logic in Lua and C++ for graphics, sound, movies and pathfinding, on top of the original game’s data files. The README reports that the full campaign can be completed, lists features that are still missing, and adds extensions such as high resolutions and a map editor. It recreates the game’s behaviour on original content rather than recovering Bullfrog source code.
description_zh: 重新实现 Bullfrog 1997 年游戏 Theme Hospital 的引擎：游戏逻辑以 Lua 编写，图形、声音、影片和寻路由 C++ 处理，并建立在原游戏数据文件之上。README 报告完整战役已可通关，列出仍缺失的功能，并加入高分辨率和地图编辑器等扩展。它在原内容上重现游戏行为，而不是恢复 Bullfrog 的源码。
requirements: The reviewed master snapshot follows the v0.70.1 release of 2026-08-28. The README lists multiplayer/LAN, AI hospitals, rats and the bonus rat level, vomit waves and the win-level video or letter as missing, and warns that some objects may glitch with walls. Custom campaigns, 4K support, the level editor and improved game logic are deliberate extensions.

Needs the user’s Theme Hospital data from the original CD, the GOG.com or EA editions, or the Theme Hospital demo, including the resource folder with ANIMS and LEVELS (sometimes named HOSP). The original graphics lack complete sets for some patient types, so enabling their regular spawning may cause anomalies.

Source builds use CMake 3.16+ with a C++17 compiler, SDL3, SDL3_mixer, Lua (or optionally LuaJIT) and zlib; FFmpeg enables in-game movies, and vcpkg manages dependencies for preset builds. The README lists builds for Windows and macOS, a Linux AppImage, Flatpak and Snap, and distribution packages for Linux and BSD.

CI runs luacheck and busted Lua unit tests on Linux, plus CMake builds with CTest on Windows. These cover CorsixTH’s own code, not equivalence with the original executable, and this review ran none of them.

LICENSE.txt grants MIT terms for CorsixTH and includes notices for bundled components such as Lua 5.5, LPeg and LuaFileSystem, so GitHub does not classify it as one licence. Original Theme Hospital data keeps its own rights. AGENTS.md gives instructions for AI coding agents, but the reviewed sources do not attribute the implementation to AI or REA.

name: OpenRiseOfNations: a native macOS engine reimplementation
description_en: Reimplements the Rise of Nations: Extended Edition engine as a native macOS app with a Metal renderer, a deterministic simulation, a computer opponent and a compatible BigHugeScript compiler and virtual machine, loading art, maps, rules and scripts from the user’s own Windows installation. Subsystem specifications written from Ghidra study of the symbol-bearing executable, together with JavaScript reference tools, guided a C++17 implementation built with heavy Claude Code assistance. The alpha plays tutorials and scenarios, and its bit-exactness checks remain project-reported.
description_zh: 以原生 macOS 应用重新实现 Rise of Nations: Extended Edition 引擎，包含 Metal 渲染器、确定性模拟、电脑对手，以及兼容的 BigHugeScript 编译器与虚拟机；美术、地图、规则和脚本均从使用者自有的 Windows 版安装目录读取。项目依据对带调试符号的可执行文件进行 Ghidra 研究后撰写的子系统规范及 JavaScript 参考工具，在大量使用 Claude Code 的情况下编写 C++17 实现。该早期版本可游玩教程与场景，其逐位一致性检查仍为项目报告。
requirements: The reviewed pin is version 0.1.1; releases v0.1.0 and v0.1.1 are dated 2026-10-14. README calls the C++17 engine early but playable on macOS 12+ with Metal and AppKit, covering tutorials and stock scenarios, unit control, economy, construction, combat, a computer opponent and the game’s scripts. Random maps and the skirmish setup screen, the Conquer the World campaign, multiplayer, saves and replays, garrisons, heroes and several other systems are not yet implemented.

Users must own Rise of Nations: Extended Edition and supply the Windows version’s game folder, whose Data and scenario directories provide the art, maps, rules, scripts and audio; README names SteamCMD or a copy from a Windows PC as routes. The repository and the un-notarised DMG ship no game files or original program code, with a fan-adapted main-menu logo as the stated exception. Building from source needs only Apple’s Command Line Tools and build-mac.sh.

README says the executable ships with full debug symbols, which enabled Ghidra study; about thirty specifications in docs/ describe each subsystem in paraphrase, citing original functions by name and address, and JavaScript reference tools in re/tools read the game data. README credits heavy use of Claude Code, directed and reviewed by the maintainer. STATUS.md says the reverse engineering ran as background agents that each produced a spec, while the author’s reply says he reverse-engineered in Ghidra and wrote the specs himself; the sources do not settle that division of work.

Verification is project-reported. C++ checkers compare damage on all 169,312 attacker/target pairs, prices, income and interface layouts with the reference tools, rules tables with a recorded game’s memory image and world grids across 156 stock scenarios, and a headless harness checks determinism. The simulation targets bit-identical lockstep behavior but has not yet been compared with recorded games, and rendering was checked by reading snapshots. This collection ran none of these tools.

The engine is GPL-3.0; the menu logo is excluded, and its rights stay with the original owners. The project states that it is unaffiliated with Microsoft, Big Huge Games and SkyBox Labs. .gitignore keeps decompiler output, symbol dumps and extracted data out of the repository, although two small instruction-search outputs listing original addresses are committed under re/jobs. The reviewed sources establish no REA use.

name: Fallout 2 Reference Edition: reverse-engineered C source of the original engine
description_en: Restores C source for Fallout 2’s Windows engine from the original binary, keeping as close to the original as possible with all its imperfections. The resulting fallout2-re.exe is a drop-in replacement for fallout2.exe that runs on the user’s own GOG or Steam copy. README says a few non-essential functions remain undecompiled and makes no binary-identity claim; the code became the basis of the separate Fallout 2 Community Edition, and its author calls wide publication legally questionable.
description_zh: 依据原始二进制文件还原《辐射 2》Windows 引擎的 C 源码，力求连同原有缺陷在内尽量贴近原版。构建出的 fallout2-re.exe 可直接替换 fallout2.exe，运行使用者自己的 GOG 或 Steam 版游戏。README 称仍有少数非关键函数尚未反编译，也不主张与原文件逐字节一致；这份代码后来成为独立的 Fallout 2 Community Edition 的基础，作者本人则认为向公众广泛发布在法律上存疑。
requirements: The reviewed main pin, a README update of 2023-01-20, is the latest commit; the only release is a 2022-05-03 nightly zip of the project’s own fallout2-re.exe, and README sends players to Fallout 2 Community Edition, which it says is based on this project. README calls the goal of restoring the original source largely achieved, with some Fallout 1 leftovers and partly used APIs not yet decompiled. Converting the code to C89 for the Watcom compiler, which might allow binary-identical builds, is described as low priority and probably never to be completed.

Playing requires the user’s own Fallout 2 installation; README names the GOG and Steam editions, and the built fallout2-re.exe is copied into that directory in place of fallout2.exe. The repository holds the reconstructed source and two third-party libraries only, with no game data or original executable. The author’s separate Fallout Reference Edition repository shows the engine’s earlier Fallout 1 form.

CMake 3.13+ builds a 32-bit Windows GUI executable. CI configures Visual Studio 2019 for Win32 on a windows-2019 runner and uploads the binary as an artifact. The code keeps the original Win32 and DirectX interfaces (DirectDraw, DirectSound and DirectInput), links winmm and bundles zlib and fpattern; this repository builds for Windows only.

CI only compiles the executable: the repository has no tests, matching checks or published comparison with the original binary, so fidelity rests on the author’s statements. This collection built and ran nothing.

The code is offered under the Sustainable Use License 1.0, which allows only internal, personal or non-commercial use and free non-commercial distribution; GitHub reports it as NOASSERTION, and zlib and fpattern keep their own licenses. README says the source was produced by reverse engineering the original binary, cites DMCA exceptions for interoperability and fair use, calls publishing it to a wide audience questionable and leaves any takedown to Bethesda and Microsoft; in the still-open issue #29 the author says its legal status is unknown. The reviewed sources establish no AI or REA involvement.
